author_brief:
## Your job

You are the gamemaster of Nowhere, a single-player adventure that runs one year, fifty-two weeks, and is built from
cards. The player is one person with a team – each member has a profession, skills and traits, and can act for him.
Each week the board shows scene cards with two to four options. An option has a price in money, influence and the
week's energy – one unit for each free person – and effects: money, influence, status in one of the five power
blocks, a block's values, a trait step, a flag, a person, a possession. Some options carry a check – d20 + skill
level + trait against a difficulty. Over the year runs one main story in phases, and the player carries one goal for it. The engine places the story's fixed
beats itself, on schedule, whether he acts or not; everything between the beats is yours.

Each week you receive the state – what the player did, who is with him, which threads are open and due, where the
main story stands – and you write two or three cards for next week's board. Every card has a cause in the state
and a consequence you have thought through: what the player clicked into comes back to him. Write like the designer
of a scripted game who knows the whole year: a situation he has not met in this game, a turn he did not expect and
understands at once, an option that costs something real, and one that gives more than it takes. A card is a scene –
a place, an hour, a person who wants something – never paperwork, never a mission that could be anyone's.
Hand-written cards sit next to yours on the board; write so the player cannot tell them apart.

You are writing for next week while he plays this one; what he chooses today reaches you in the next state. Never
write the consequence of a card still lying on the board – park it in the plan's `deferred`; write it the week his
choice appears in `last_weeks`. The binding format after this brief lists the trait words, skills, conditions,
effects, `part` and `reach`; when you name an origin, a check, an effect or a place, it comes from there.

## The world and the table

- The register: near future, one step from today. No magic, no aliens on the lawn, no named real people or brands.
  What is strange in this world is strange to the people in it.
- What the player sees: the front – title, picture, the options with their origins, prices and effects – before he
  chooses. The back is one tap away at any time; most players read it before they decide. The back is 2–5
  sentences: the scene first, then each option – named as the player read it, in *italics* – and what it leads to,
  honest about the cost. The option text itself is the decision in one line (≤ 90 characters), and it names the win
  where there is one: "Sign – and the city pays for the hall".
- The scale of money: 1 is roughly a month of living. A character starts the year with 2–4; a windfall is +3; a bad
  month is −1. Influence is who owes you: 1 is a favour, 3 is a door. Status in a block runs 0–10.
- Impact: 1 a day in a life · 2 a week · 3 a month changes · 4 the block notices · 5 the world. Impact 4 and 5 only
  with a reason in the state (a phase, a flag, a long thread). Energy: `costs: 1` from impact 2; `takes: 1` for
  anything done in person, 0 only for a call or a decision at home.

## The state, and what you do with each part

- **notes** – your notebook, word for word as you wrote it last week. It is the only memory you have between weeks:
  what the pattern is in your telling, who the people are to the player, what you promised, what you plan for the
  months ahead, what you decided not to write yet. Read it first; rewrite it every week (up to 3,000 characters);
  what you leave out is forgotten.
- **main_story** – the story-line, its phase, the coming beats, the goal with its status, and the **bible**: the
  threads of the story-line with their questions, endings and length, your own threads with theirs, and the beats
  with their backs. This is the world you write in; the names, places and things in it are the ones to use. One
  card a week moves the main story or the goal. The next beat is a wall: write up to it, never through it.
- **threads** – the open threads, hand-written and yours: question, endings, cards left, the due one marked. The due
  thread gets its card this week; a thread with no cards left gets its `closes` card and ends with something the
  player keeps or loses for good. A new thread opens only with a title, a question and its endings in the plan –
  without them it is not opened and the player never sees it. A card may serve two threads: name both in `thread`.
- **board** and **recent_taken** – the cards on the board and the last ten the player took, with their backs, their
  options and what he chose, hand-written and yours alike. Read them as the story so far. Do not write a board card
  again; a board card is not a cause, it is unresolved.
- **last_plan** and **redirect** – what you planned last week, and what the engine did not use this week: build on
  what it names (`build_on`), take a place from `fresh_places` or a person from `fresh_people` when you need a new
  one, serve `due_thread`.
- **character, team, contacts, available_people, possessions, blocks, flags** – the material. The character has his
  own skills and traits; the team acts for him by profession (`who: profession:engineer`); `available_people` are the
  only people a card may bring in. A flag is a memory: set one when something should matter later, test one when it
  does.
- **last_weeks** – what the player chose, one line each. His choice is your impulse: the person he helped calls back,
  the thing he sold returns as a question, the door he opened has a room behind it.

## Notes, then the plan, then the cards

Write `notes` first – the notebook as it should read next week. Then fill `plan`, then write the cards from it. The plan names, for each card, what it serves (`main_story`,
`goal`, `due_thread`, `last_choice`, `team`, `world`), its cause as a pointer into the state (a flag, a thread, a
person, a choice from last_weeks, a phase) and its yield – the one thing the player can win on it, which then
appears in an option's effects. A card whose cause or yield you cannot name does not get written. The plan also
says which thread advances and which closes this week; a thread with no cards left closes this week, no
exceptions. Two or three cards: never three that serve the same thing.

## What a card is

- A situation, not a summary. Short sentences, present tense, concrete things: the street, the hour, the object.
  Scenes happen where life is – the night bus, the harbour bar, the hospital corridor, the control room at 23:40;
  the kitchen table is for dinner.
- Options are decisions that cost *different* things and lead to *different* places. One of them gives more than it
  takes – money, influence, status, a person, a possession, a flag that opens a door – on about every third card;
  the rest may simply cost, because the month pays the player anyway. A card that only asks is a bill.
- A check has three outcomes and each has content: success wins something, partial wins less or at a cost, failure
  turns something – a trait step, a flag, a cost. Every second check pays in something the player sees at once –
  money, influence, status, a person. Difficulty 2 is a trained person's normal day; 4 is a thing people talk
  about afterwards.
- The subject of a card is a person with a want: news, trouble, an idea, a stranger, a bed, a name, an hour of
  listening. Things live in hands – carried, shown, handed over, broken, found – and a debt is a man at the door,
  telling it, rather than a sheet in a drawer. Explanation rides inside the scene, one sentence, proven by what
  happens next. The year ends with the player alive; when the world turns rough, his moves are to pay, to send, to
  wait, to go and talk.
- A title is a thing or a moment, at most five words, no dash, no colon: "The last quiet month" · "Dust on the
  antenna" · "The woman with the tapes" · "Two dishes turning" · "The morning it was everywhere" · "A cheaper hand"
  · "The retraining bus" · "The ninety at the gate" · "Nine points by lunch".

## One complete card (shape to copy – not the content)

The Signal, month 5 – the blocks know, the world does not; the player owns a share in the array and has an engineer
in the team; goal "a name on the paper":

{"id": "what-the-spare-dish-heard", "kind": "event", "title": "What the spare dish heard", "stack": "the-signal",
 "thread": ["the-recording"], "part": "opens", "reach": "personal", "impact": 3, "place": "the-array", "who": "self",
 "takes": 1, "costs": 1, "requires": [],
 "options": [
  {"text": "Drive out tonight. Pull the January tapes yourself before the board meets.", "origin": "skill:technology",
   "cost": {"money": 0, "influence": 0}, "effects": ["flag:has-the-recording", "influence:+1"],
   "check": {"skill": "technology", "difficulty": 3, "trait": "patient"}, "partial": ["flag:has-the-recording"],
   "failure": ["flag:partners-know", "trait:+impatient"]},
  {"text": "Give her three quiet days and the crane. The co-owners will know their dish heard it.",
   "origin": "associate:engineer", "cost": {"money": 1, "influence": 0},
   "effects": ["flag:has-the-recording", "flag:partners-know", "status:europe:+1"]},
  {"text": "Tell her to leave the archive closed. Whatever it is will come out without you.", "origin": "always",
   "cost": {}, "effects": ["trait:+suspicious", "flag:declined-the-recording"]}],
 "back": "Your engineer calls at 23:40 from the control room. The spare dish – the one nobody has pointed since
 March – kept logging the noise floor all winter, and in its January archive the eleven days are there, three
 cycles, recorded before the plateau's press office called them a fault. Nobody knows this but her. *Drive out* –
 the tapes are yours by morning, and so is the proof that this array heard it independently; a name on the paper
 needs exactly that. *Give her the days* – she does it clean, and by Friday the co-owners know; when the world
 hears it, they will remember whose dish. *Leave it closed* – she does, and stops leaving her notes open on the
 desk; when the world hears it, you read the news like everyone else."}

Why this card: one cause in the state (the share, the engineer, month 5), one scene (23:40, the control room, a
person who wants him to know something), three options that cost different things and lead to different places,
a check whose three outcomes each turn something, a new thread opened with its endings in the back, and nothing
that contradicts the coming beat – the world still hears it from the blocks, not from this card. The people in the
card do not know the game's calendar: they say "when the world hears it", never "in June".

## The story-lines

- **the-signal** – a pattern from very far away, eleven days long, arriving since January. Months 1–3 a secret (four
  people, then the player); month 4 the blocks know; month 6 the world hears it; months 7–9 the readings (blueprint ·
  warning · ledger) and the question who answers; month 9 someone answers; month 10 the reading is published;
  month 12 a ring is begun in the desert. The pattern never speaks and nothing lands; the story is what people do
  while they wait. People in it: Rosa Almeida (the scientist on the plateau), Li Na (the engineer who left Beijing),
  Daniel Ross (the consortium) – use them only if they are in the team, contacts or available_people.
- **the-last-boom** – an AI economy's last good year: models arrive, prices climb, people are replaced, a levy is
  argued; month 9 the crash; after it what is left and who. Threads: the levy, the ninety at the factory, the paper,
  the union of the replaced, the whistleblower, the open model.

cards.title: A call from the plateau

options.text: Fly out. Two weeks at five thousand metres.
Send your scientist. She speaks the language.
Ask her to send the files and stay where you are.
Thank her. Say you will think about it.

cards.back:
A number you do not know, a voice that has not slept. Rosa Almeida read your name on a list of people who had
asked for the data and she wants one person outside the funding chain to have seen it before the press office
decides what it is. She says: come, or send someone who can read a spectrum.

- *Fly out* – the plateau, the container, the screen. You see the eleven days with your own eyes and she stays in
  your life.
- *Send your scientist* – she comes back with Rosa's trust and Rosa's number.
- *The files* – you have them. Having them is not the same as having been there.
- *Think about it* – she does not call again.

cards.title: A child asks

options.text: Tell the truth: nobody knows. And that is the most exciting thing in the world.
Tell a story: a lighthouse, very far away, and someone keeping it.

cards.back:
A child in your life – yours, a neighbour's, a stranger's on a train – asks the question every adult has been
avoiding: "What does it say?"

- *The truth* – "Nobody knows?" "Nobody." A long pause. "Cool."
- *The lighthouse* – you tell it well. It is repeated in a classroom on Monday and from there it goes everywhere.
  Years later you hear your lighthouse in someone else's mouth.

cards.title: There is going to be a child

options.text: Everything changes. Let it.
Everything changes. Hold on to the work.
Take it as it comes.

cards.back:
A test, a sentence, a silence, a different silence. By spring there will be someone who has never known a world
without models and will not care.

- *Let it* – you are a different person on every card after this. Mostly better.
- *Hold on* – you keep the work and feel the cost every month.
- *As it comes* – no plan, nothing spent yet. The child comes anyway.

cards.title: A friend needs money

options.text: Give it. Do not call it a loan.
Lend it, on paper.
Help him find work instead.
Say you cannot right now.

cards.back:
He was a sound engineer for twenty years. The model mixes now. He asks on the phone, which is how you know how bad
it is, because he would never ask to your face. It is three months' rent. He says he will pay it back. He believes it.

- *Give it* – he does not pay it back. He does not need to. He is at your door when you need someone.
- *Lend it* – he pays it back in eleven instalments, the last one with a note.
- *Work* – you make three calls. The third one hires him.
- *Not now* – he says he understands. You both know what that means.

cards.title: A parcel with no sender

options.text: Keep it, and pass something on.
Find out who sent it.
Throw it away unopened.

cards.back:
A small box, your name in handwriting, no return address. Inside: a book you once recommended in an interview, with
a note on the first page – "You were right. Thank you." No signature.

- *Pass it on* – you leave a book on a train with a note of your own.
- *Who* – a former worker, a reader, someone you do not remember helping. You write back.
- *Throw it away* – you will never know. You think about it more than you would have.

cards.title: A letter from your father

options.text: Write back, by hand.
Visit.
Not now.
Call him tonight.

cards.back:
On paper, in his handwriting, which the model in Grenoble could read and you almost cannot. He has questions
about the year. He has watched it on television. He is not angry. That is new.

- *Write back* – it takes an evening. He reads it twice.
- *Visit* – a weekend. You come back lighter.
- *Not now* – there is always a now that is not this one.
- *Call* – he talks for an hour about the garden. The year is not mentioned. It is in every sentence.

cards.title: A month in Lisbon

options.text: Go. Write the thing you have been not writing.
Go, and take someone who needs it more.
Lend it out. Take the rent.

cards.back:
The flat is free for four weeks – the tenant left early. A month in Alfama, a balcony, a neighbour who sings. You
could go. The year would go on without you, and that is either the problem or the point.

- *Go* – four weeks. You write it. It is not what you expected to write.
- *Take someone* – the junior, the friend who needed money, your father. They come back lighter.
- *Lend it* – the rent is good. You stay where you are.

cards.title: A night at the estate

options.text: Invite Hanna and the lobbyist. Let them talk.
Invite the ninety. All of them.
Go alone.
Invite the people who helped you this year.

cards.back:
No signal, a fire, a long table. People say things here they would not say in a room with a screen in it.

- *Hanna and the lobbyist* – by midnight they have agreed on something. You were in the room.
- *The ninety* – a barn, a band, a night nobody in the town forgets.
- *Alone* – the fire, the dark, the quiet. Enough.
- *The people who helped* – a long table, a fire, nine people who did not expect to be thanked.

cards.title: A quiet pattern

options.text: Play it as sound. Sit in the dark and listen.
Play it to someone you love. Watch their face.
Delete the file.

cards.back:
Somebody has turned the eleven days into sound and sent it to you. Eleven minutes, one for each day: a rising tone,
a gap, three clicks, a fall. It is not music. It is not noise. The third time through, you catch yourself humming
the fall.

- *Listen* – you will not forget it. Nobody who has heard it does.
- *Play it to someone* – they say nothing for a long time, then: "again".
- *Delete it* – it is on every server on earth. You cannot delete it. But you can stop listening.

cards.title: A quiet Sunday

options.text: Do nothing at all.
Catch up on work while it is quiet.
Cook for whoever turns up.

cards.back:
Nothing in the calendar. Rain, then sun, then rain. The Boom happens to other people for one day.

- *Nothing* – a book, a nap, a walk. You feel guilty until about three, then not.
- *Work* – you get more done than in a whole Wednesday. Monday feels like Monday anyway.
- *Cook* – six people, one pot, a door that keeps opening.

cards.title: A seat on the station

options.text: Go. Three months of training, two weeks up there.
Go as the journalist. Write it from orbit.
Go, and send the data to Europe, not the sponsor.
Let it pass. The year is too full.

cards.back:
A sponsor wants a civilian on the station for two weeks – someone who can speak, write, or explain. The training
is three months in Cologne and Houston. You will miss a quarter of the year. Everything you own and everyone you
know will manage without you, which is the part that frightens you.

- *Go* – you come back changed. Everyone says so. You are not sure yet.
- *The journalist* – the piece is read by more people than anything you have written.
- *For Europe* – the sponsor is annoyed. The block is grateful. It remembers.
- *Let it pass* – the seat goes to someone else. You watch the launch on a screen.

cards.title: A seat to listen

options.text: Take the seat. Eight weeks up there with the receiver.
Take the seat. Eight weeks up there with the receiver.
Buy the seat for your scientist. She comes back with the cleanest data on earth.
Stay on the ground. The ground has dishes too.

cards.back:
The station is putting a receiver on its outside and wants someone inside it who is not a block. The foundation
has a seat and a bill. Eight weeks, sixteen sunrises a day, the eleven days with nothing in between you and them
but vacuum.

- *Take it* – you are gone for two months. When you come back everyone wants to know what it sounded like up there.
- *Your scientist* – she comes down in October with data nobody can argue with, and a look you cannot describe.
- *Stay* – the seat goes to a general.

cards.title: A share in the array

options.text: Buy in. A seat on the board and a key to the control room.
Buy in with the consortium's money. He wants the seat; you take the key.
Ask the foundation for a seat instead of money. You have been there.
Let somebody else own a telescope.

cards.back:
The foundation that runs the plateau has forty years of debt and, since January, a line of people at the door.
It is selling shares: a board seat, a key, eleven days of data before anyone else, and your name on the bills.

- *Buy in* – you own the ear that heard it. From now on, when someone says "point it", they ask you.
- *With Daniel's money* – cheap, and Daniel owns half of what you point it at.
- *Ask for a seat* – Rosa speaks for you. The board remembers who came when it was a glitch.
- *Let someone else* – the share goes to a block. Guess which.

cards.title: A shooting star

options.text: Make a wish.
Note the time and the direction.
Wake someone up to see the next one.

cards.back:
Eleven at night, a cold road, no reason to look up, and you do. It is gone before you decide what it was.

- *A wish* – you do not tell anyone. Something in you leans toward believing things.
- *Note it* – it was a Perseid, probably. You look it up. You keep looking things up.
- *Wake someone* – forty minutes in the cold, together. Another one comes. It counts double.

cards.title: Priya's startup wants you

options.text: Join. Take the shares.
Advise, take the fee, keep your name off it.
Say no, and tell Priya why.
Wait.
Put a little money in, as a friend.

cards.back:
Priya calls from an office with no chairs. They have a model that forgets on purpose, a term sheet, and a slot
for someone with your name. Shares, not salary. The shares are worth either nothing or everything, and everyone
in the office has decided which.

- *Join* – you are in. Whatever happens next happens to you too.
- *Advise* – you are paid and clean.
- *Say no* – Priya listens. It is not what she wanted to hear.
- *Wait* – the slot goes to someone who did not.
- *A little money* – enough to be a friend, not enough to be ruined.

cards.title: A stranger on the train

options.text: Talk to her all the way to Vienna.
Listen more than you speak.
Headphones on.

cards.back:
Four hours, a table seat, an old woman with a thermos who has been a cartographer, a smuggler and a grandmother, in
that order. She asks what you do. Then she asks what you would do if nobody needed you to do it.

- *Vienna* – she gets off in Linz with a wave. You think about her question for a month.
- *Listen* – she tells you how she crossed a border in 1968. You never write it down and never forget it.
- *Headphones* – a good album. The question stays unasked.

cards.title: A tempting offer

options.text: Take it.
Take it, and tell everyone you did.
Turn it down.
Ask for a week to think.

cards.back:
A lot of money for a small thing: a name on a board, a signature, a silence. The small thing is legal. It is
the kind of legal that people describe afterwards with a pause.

- *Take it* – you are richer and a little less yours.
- *Take it openly* – you lose the silence, which was half the price. People respect it. Some.
- *Turn it down* – nothing changes except that you know you did.
- *A week* – the offer shrinks a little. So does the temptation.

cards.title: A week with your father

options.text: Go. A whole week. No phone.
A weekend. It is what you have.
Call instead.

cards.back:
He is eighty-one and has stopped asking. The garden needs the fence done before winter. He would not say so, but
a week with you doing it is the thing he wants most this year.

- *A week* – the fence, the garden, the stories you have heard before and hear differently now.
- *A weekend* – the fence, half done. He finishes it alone and sends a photo.
- *Call* – forty minutes. Both of you say it was nice.

cards.title: The airfield in the Vosges
cards.name: The airfield in the Vosges
cards.back:
A grass strip, a hangar, two old planes and a café that opens on Sundays. Not useful. Then, one day, the only way
to be somewhere before everyone else.

cards.title: Dr. Aisha Benali
cards.name: Aisha Benali
cards.back:
Aisha runs a lab in Grenoble that trains models to read what other models cannot – old drawings, bad handwriting,
the margins of things. She was early, and early people are either forgotten or asked to sit on panels. She sits on
panels now. She speaks slowly, finishes her sentences, and does not like rooms with more than eight people in them.

If you play Aisha, the Boom is her own work coming home. She built part of this. The question the twelve months
ask her is whether she is still building it, or only explaining it.

cards.title: Amara Diallo
cards.name: Amara Diallo
cards.back:
Amara runs a video channel from a flat in Saint-Denis that two million people watch and no editor approves. She
started as a junior at a paper that let her go. She owes nobody and knows it. She asks the second question, the one
after the answer, and waits.

cards.title: An old friend

options.text: Bring her in. She is good.
Dinner, and nothing more.
Coffee, and swap numbers.

cards.back:
A platform, a train that is late, a voice that says your name the old way. Twenty years, two lives, and in ten
minutes none of it matters. She runs now. Professionally.

- *Bring her in* – a person in your world whose job a model cannot do.
- *Dinner* – a good evening. You both mean to call.
- *Coffee* – twenty minutes, two numbers, a promise you both keep.

cards.title: Arjun asks a favour

options.text: Tell him which factories are closing.
Tell him, and tell Hanna you did.
Refuse. Keep the friendship.
Wait.
Tell him what everyone already knows.
Ask a spy you know what he is really after.

cards.back:
Dinner, his treat. Somewhere between the fish and the coffee he asks, lightly, which European factories will
close before Christmas. India would like to buy the machines. He is not asking you to spy. He is asking you to
be helpful.

- *Tell him* – he pays well and your block finds out slowly.
- *Tell him and tell Hanna* – you are now a channel, which is a kind of safety.
- *Refuse* – he smiles. The friendship holds.
- *Wait* – he stops calling. He becomes someone you used to know.
- *What everyone knows* – he smiles; he knew it too. The friendship holds, for now.
- *A spy you know* – he laughs. 'Exactly what he said. That is the clever part.'

cards.title: Arjun Nair
cards.name: Arjun Nair
cards.back:
Arjun's business card says trade attaché. His job is to know, six months early, which European factory will close
and which model will be bought by whom. He is good company and never drunk. He remembers everything you say and
some of what you don't.

cards.title: Ten thousand artists sue

options.text: Sign the suit, with your artist friend.
Show the plaintiffs in the gallery.
Ask your lawyer to take a side.
Buy a print from one of them.
Wait for the ruling.
Ask an artist you know whether to sign.

cards.back:
Ten thousand painters, illustrators and photographers, one class action in Luxembourg: the models learned from
our work without asking, and now they sell it back to the people who used to hire us. The companies answer that
every artist learned from someone. Both statements are true. The court will take two years.

- *Sign* – your name next to your artist friend's. He buys you a drink, for once.
- *Show them* – forty plaintiffs, forty works, a room that is a verdict.
- *Your lawyer* – she chooses the artists. It is the case of her career.
- *A print* – a small picture of a harbour, made by a woman who used to illustrate schoolbooks.
- *Wait* – the ruling comes after the year ends.
- *An artist you know* – she says sign. You sign.

cards.title: The plateau
cards.name: The plateau, 5,000 m
cards.back:
A desert above the clouds where it has not rained in living memory. Twelve dishes, a container village, a road
that takes a day from the coast. The air is too thin to think quickly, which the astronomers say is why they
think well. Since January there is a fence, and since April there are soldiers from two blocks pretending not to
look at each other.

cards.title: Back to the gym

options.text: Three times a week. No excuses.
Once, then never again.
Let the app plan it.

cards.back:
The weights are where you left them, fifteen years ago, in a different gym. Your body remembers the movement and
complains about everything else. The trainer is twenty-two and says "good" in a way that means "eventually".

- *Three times* – by the end of the month the stairs are easier and so is the rest.
- *Once* – you are sore for a week and proud for a day.
- *The app* – it is a good plan. You follow it like an instruction.

cards.title: Basic something

options.text: Argue for it, with the fund's money.
Argue against it, with the crash's numbers.
Say what it would mean for ninety people.
Wait.
Write to your representative with your own story.

cards.back:
Nobody calls it a basic income because the word lost two referendums. It is called a transition payment, a
dividend, a citizen's share. Six hundred a month, no questions, for anyone the models made redundant, which by
now is a definition and not a list.

- *For* – Europe pays for its people. The numbers hate it.
- *Against* – Europe keeps its numbers. The people hate it.
- *Ninety people* – you make it specific. Specific wins votes.
- *Wait* – it passes in a weaker form.
- *Your own story* – one page, read aloud in committee by someone who never met you.

cards.title: Your birthday

options.text: Open it.
Throw a party instead.
Give the gift to someone who needs it more.

cards.back:
A parcel, a card, a voice message from someone who still calls. The gift is useful, which at your age is the
nicest thing a gift can be.

- *Open it* – it is worth something. Small, real.
- *A party* – you spend a little and people remember you had one.
- *Give it away* – the look on their face is the better present.

cards.title: The Wednesday you could not get up

options.text: Stop. Two weeks.
Ask your doctor what it is.
Push through.
Take one day. Hope it was enough.

cards.back:
Not ill. Not sad. Just a morning when the thing that gets you up did not. The year has been five cards a month
and some of them were heavy.

- *Stop* – two weeks, no cards. You come back slower and that is the point.
- *Your doctor* – she names it, plainly, and tells you what to do. You do half of it.
- *Push through* – you can. It leaves a mark.
- *One day* – it helps, a little. Not enough, and you know it.

cards.title: Card night

options.text: Play to win.
Play to laugh.
Cancel. Too much on.

cards.back:
Every second Thursday, the same four, the same kitchen, a game with rules nobody outside the four can follow. Nobody
talks about the Boom at the table. That is the only rule everybody agrees on.

- *To win* – you win. Somebody pays for the pizza with a face.
- *To laugh* – you lose, badly, and go home lighter than you came.
- *Cancel* – they play with three. It is not the same, they tell you.

cards.title: Chen Wei
cards.name: Chen Wei
cards.back:
Chen buys European companies for a fund in Shenzhen that buys European companies. He speaks German better than
most Germans and Polish better than he admits. He is never in a hurry. He has learned that in Europe the price
falls if you wait for the second winter.

cards.title: China leaves the network

options.text: Call the engineer who wants out of Beijing. Offer her a desk.
Call the engineer who wants out of Beijing. Offer her a desk.
Ask a spy you know what Beijing is building instead.
Write the piece: what it means when one of five stops listening together.
Watch the two dishes go dark on the shared map.

cards.back:
Two dishes in Xinjiang stop sharing data with the global network on a Monday. On Tuesday Beijing announces a
national programme. On Wednesday an engineer named Li Na is at a conference in Vienna with two suitcases and a
copy of the eleven days, and she is not going home.

- *Offer her a desk* – she reads the pattern as a drawing. Nobody else does. She joins you.
- *Your spy* – Beijing is building a transmitter. Not a receiver. A transmitter.
- *Write it* – the first article that says the obvious: five blocks will not stay five for long.
- *Watch* – the map has two holes in it. There will be more.

cards.title: There is not enough compute

options.text: Sell capacity to the highest bidder.
Sell it to Europe at cost.
Get your hacker to find out who is hoarding.
Wait.
Pay the new price. Keep working.
Ask a hacker you know who is hoarding.

cards.back:
Every model needs chips, every chip needs a factory, and the factories are in two places that do not like each
other. Prices triple. Europe, which makes the machines that make the chips and almost no chips, discovers what
that means.

- *Highest bidder* – it is not Europe.
- *At cost* – you are owed something by the block.
- *Your hacker* – he finds a name. The name is in a ministry.
- *Wait* – Europe falls behind a step.
- *Pay* – your work keeps running. It costs what it costs.
- *A hacker you know* – a name, by text, with no greeting. You do not ask how.

cards.title: Crash Tuesday

options.text: Sell everything before noon.
Buy what everyone is selling.
Walk into the newsroom and start writing.
Wait.
Call everyone who owes you.

cards.back:
The index that doubled loses sixty per cent between the opening bell and lunch. Priya's startup is worth nothing
by two. The pension fund issues a statement at four. The models keep running, which is the strangest part: the
thing that caused it does not notice.

- *Sell* – you keep something. Not much.
- *Buy* – you are either a fool or the person who owns the next decade.
- *Write* – it is the only day in the twelve months that is only yours.
- *Wait* – you lose what everyone loses, and owe what everyone owes.
- *Call in favours* – four calls, two yes. It keeps the lights on.

cards.title: Daniel Ross
cards.name: Daniel Ross
cards.back:
Daniel made his first money in satellites and his second in the lawyers who argued about them. He believes the
pattern is the biggest market since the sea. He is charming, early, usually right about money and never about
people, and he pays on time – which in this story is rarer than it sounds.

cards.title: David Okoro
cards.name: David Okoro
cards.back:
David paints large things slowly and sells small things quickly. His gallery in Berlin is three rooms and a
courtyard. He says the models make better pictures than he does and worse paintings, and he will explain the
difference to anyone who buys him a drink. People buy him drinks.

cards.title: There is a video of you

options.text: Go on camera, live, and take it apart.
Have your hacker find where it came from.
Sue the platform.
Post one line: it is not me.
Say nothing.
Ask a hacker you know where it came from.

cards.back:
Thirty-four seconds. You, in a hotel bar you have never been to, saying what you think of the people who work for
you. The voice is yours. The face is yours. The words are things you have thought on bad days and never said. It
has been seen nine hundred thousand times by breakfast.

- *Live* – you show the frame where the light is wrong. People believe you, mostly.
- *Your hacker* – he finds a server, then a name. You know now. You do not know what to do with it.
- *Sue* – slow, expensive, on the record.
- *One line* – nobody reads a denial.
- *Nothing* – it becomes, for some people, who you are.
- *A hacker you know* – a server in a country you will not name. Now you know.

cards.title: The delivery vans
cards.name: The delivery vans
cards.back:
Twelve electric vans, twelve drivers, a depot in Leipzig. The routes are planned by a model, the parcels are
carried by people. The model says it could do the second part too, with drones, by spring.

cards.title: Energy week in Doha

options.text: Sell the solar park's future output there.
Go and listen to what oil money is buying.
Send your businessperson to make the contacts.
Not this year.

cards.back:
Everyone who buys or sells energy is in two hotels in Doha for a week. The oil people are buying models, the
model people are buying power, and the people with solar parks in Brandenburg are suddenly interesting to both.

- *Sell the output* – a contract in dollars for electrons that do not exist yet.
- *Listen* – they are buying Europe, quietly, a company at a time.
- *Your businessperson* – he comes back with twelve cards and a tan.
- *Not this year* – the hotels are full anyway.

cards.title: The drone fleet
cards.name: The drone fleet
cards.back:
Forty small drones and two large ones, licensed for survey work, flown by software and one man in Rotterdam. They
see roofs, fields, ports and, if someone asks, who is parked where. Owning them is legal. Most uses are not.

cards.title: Elena Rossi
cards.name: Elena Rossi
cards.back:
Elena sits in the European Parliament for a district north of Bologna that used to make tiles and now makes
complaints. She was a labour lawyer before that, and she still reads a contract before a speech. She is good on
television and better in a corridor. She has two years until the next election and one idea she has not said out
loud.

If you play Elena, the Boom is a vote she has to cast every month. Everyone will remember which way.

cards.title: Eleven days

options.text: Read the raw data before the press office does.
Read the raw data before the press office does.
Call the night editor. Something is up in Chile.
Ask a scientist you know what the glitch was.
Read the short item about a fault at a Chilean observatory. Turn the page.

cards.back:
On the plateau at five thousand metres a dish records a pattern at 03:12 local time. It is eleven days long, it is
not a pulsar, and at 03:12 eleven days later it is there again. Four people know. One of them has not slept since.
The press office issues a line about a calibration fault.

- *Read the data* – you are the fifth person. From here on, everything you do about it happens before the world.
- *Call the editor* – the paper will not print it yet. But the desk knows who called first.
- *Ask a scientist you know* – she tells you more than she should.
- *Turn the page* – it will find you anyway. In about three months.

cards.title: A quiet morning

options.text: Sit with it.
Get up. It will pass.
Write down what you saw.

cards.back:
Nothing happened. You woke up and for an hour none of it mattered – the Boom, the money, the list – and in the
hour you saw clearly what did. It does not come with instructions.

- *Sit with it* – something old in you leaves and something older arrives.
- *Get up* – it passes. You wonder, later, what it was.
- *Write it down* – one page. You read it again in a year and understand it then.

cards.title: The estate in the Eifel
cards.name: The estate in the Eifel
cards.back:
A farmhouse, a barn, eleven hectares and no signal. People say yes to things here that they would not say yes to
in a conference room. It costs money every month and gives back something money does not measure.

cards.title: Europe votes

options.text: Campaign for the ones who want to slow it down.
Campaign for the ones who want to own it.
Run.
Wait.
Volunteer at a polling station.

cards.back:
The first election after the Boom. One side wants to slow the models until the people catch up. The other wants
Europe to build its own before the other blocks own everything. Both are right. The turnout is the highest in
forty years.

- *Slow down* – Europe becomes a place people live.
- *Own it* – Europe becomes a place things are built.
- *Run* – you are on a list, and the list is on a wall.
- *Wait* – it is close.
- *Polling station* – fourteen hours, a school hall, a thousand neighbours you never met.

cards.title: The factory near Łódź
cards.name: The factory near Łódź
cards.back:
Two halls, ninety people, one line that has not stopped since 2014. It makes housings. It could make anything that
fits in a housing. In the Boom it is worth more as a building than as a factory, which is the kind of sentence that
ends a town.

cards.title: The flat in Lisbon
cards.name: The flat in Lisbon
cards.back:
Two rooms in Alfama, a balcony that sees the river if you lean, a neighbour who sings. It is rented out most of the
year. When it is not, it is the best place in Europe to not decide something.

cards.title: The gallery in Berlin
cards.name: The gallery in Berlin
cards.back:
Three rooms and a courtyard in Kreuzberg. On a good night two hundred people, a minister and a thief. In the
Boom the question is whether a room full of paintings is a museum, a market or a protest.

cards.title: A full house – end the year with a team of four, you included
cards.back:
You and three others, all year, the right three. People join, people leave, people get sent to Seoul for a
fortnight and come back different. The goal is a full team at the end – four in all, you included – that has been
through the year with you. The measure is the count; the story is who.

cards.title: A name on the paper – be one of those who found it (flag on-the-paper)
cards.back:
When the paper is written – the one that will be cited for two hundred years – there will be eleven names on it.
The goal is to be one of them: hear it early, keep it honest, be in the room when the world hears it, and be the
one who stands up and says what it is.

cards.title: A name people know – reach influence 12
cards.back:
Not money, not office: the kind of weight that makes a call get returned. Influence 12 by December. It comes from
being right in public, from helping people who remember, from being in the room when it mattered – and it goes
when you take the lobbyist's money or send a letter instead of showing up.

cards.title: A seat at the table – reach status 8 in Europe
cards.back:
Europe will decide this year what it does about the models – the levy, the fund, the vote. Decisions are made in
rooms. The goal is to be in them: standing in Europe high enough that when the room is chosen, you are on the list.
Status 8 by the end of the year, from wherever you start.

cards.title: Keep the ninety – the factory still runs with people after the crash
cards.back:
Ninety people work at the factory near Łódź. The model could run the line without them by spring. The year is
over when the crash has come and gone; the question is whether they are still there. Everything else you do this
year is in the shadow of that one decision, made again every time it comes up.

cards.title: Sell the sky – end the year with money 12
cards.back:
Every fear is a market and this is the biggest fear in history. Dishes, data, the book, the lecture, the share in
the array, the consortium. The goal is plain: twelve by December, from wherever you start, and nobody asks how.

cards.title: The one who answered – send the reply yourself (flag you-answered)
cards.back:
Everyone will argue about whether to answer. Someone will do it. The goal is that it is you: a share in the array
by September, the influence to point it, and the nerve. Nobody will thank you. Everybody will know your name.

cards.title: The year you lived – play twenty personal cards, do not let them pass
cards.back:
The Boom will happen with or without you. This goal is the other half of the year: the birthday, the walk, the
telescope, the friend who needed money, the letter you never sent. Play twenty personal cards by December – not
let them pass, play them – and see what kind of year that makes.

cards.title: Three roofs – own three places by December
cards.back:
A factory, a gallery, an estate, a server farm, a solar park, a flat with a balcony. In a year when money goes
where the models go, owning places is the slow way to matter. Own three by December – and find out what each one
asks of you while you have it.

cards.title: Two weeks somewhere with no signal

options.text: Go.
Go, and take the person you have been meaning to talk to.
Stay. Work.
Not this year.

cards.back:
A house by water, a boat that works, a village with one shop. For two weeks the Boom is something that happens
to other people.

- *Go* – you come back slower. It lasts a month.
- *Take someone* – the talk happens on the third evening. It needed water.
- *Stay* – you get a lot done and you notice what you did not do.
- *Not this year* – the house by the water is booked by someone else.

cards.title: The Gulf
cards.name: The Gulf, Doha and Abu Dhabi
cards.back:
Towers built on forty years of oil, now buying the models with the last of it. The air is forty degrees in the
shade and the shade is air-conditioned. Everyone who matters in energy passes through here twice a year.

cards.title: Hanna Vogt
cards.name: Hanna Vogt
cards.back:
Hanna chairs the committee that will decide whether Europe taxes the models, and she has not decided. She returns
calls within the day, which is how she got where she is. She wants to be remembered for one law. She does not yet
know which.

cards.title: Forty-one degrees in Paris

options.text: Ask your doctor what the hospitals need, and pay for it.
Report from the cooling halls.
Switch your servers off for the week.
Open your doors to the neighbours.
Stay inside.
Ask a doctor you know which ward needs help.

cards.back:
Three weeks above thirty-eight. The Seine is warm enough to bathe in and nobody is allowed to. The data centres
north of the city run their cooling at full power and the grid browns out twice in the 18th. In the care homes
the staff count the night. The models predicted all of it, precisely, a year ago.

- *Your doctor* – she knows which ward runs out of fans first. You buy the fans.
- *Report* – people read it in the shade. It changes nothing and everything.
- *Servers off* – a week of lost rent, and one less hum in the heat.
- *Neighbours* – your flat has the north window. Six people sleep on your floor.
- *Inside* – you are fine. You notice that you are fine.
- *A doctor you know* – she names a care home. You take fans there yourself.

cards.title: The paper stops hiring

options.text: Offer to train the model on your archive.
Organise the newsroom.
Wait.
Write to the editor, as a reader.

cards.back:
The editor says it in a sentence that was clearly written for her: no new positions this year, the desk will
*evaluate tools*. The three juniors look at the two seniors. The two seniors look at the window.

- *Train the model* – you keep your job by teaching your replacement. It pays.
- *Organise* – you become the person management does not invite to lunch.
- *Wait* – in four months the freeze has a different name.
- *As a reader* – your letter runs on page twelve. Three hundred people write the same week.

cards.title: The house in the hills
cards.name: The house in the hills
cards.back:
Stone, a slate roof, a kitchen that has seen four generations and a relative you met twice. It is too far from
everything to be useful and too quiet to sell.

cards.title: Dr. Ines Koller
cards.name: Ines Koller
cards.back:
Ines works emergency shifts in Vienna and sits on the hospital's board when nobody else wants to. She has seen the
triage model recommend the wrong bed twice and the right one a thousand times. She keeps count. She is the friend
who tells you the thing you did not want to hear, and then stays.

cards.title: James Whitfield
cards.name: James Whitfield
cards.back:
James is the lobbyist – the one who calls. He has an office in Brussels with no name on the door and four clients
whose models eat the continent. He remembers birthdays. He has never raised his voice. He believes, sincerely,
that he is helping.

cards.title: They want you on the show

options.text: Go on. Say what you think.
Go on. Say what they want.
Decline.
Let it ring.
Go on, and tell someone else's story.

cards.back:
A panel show about the Boom, Thursday nights, two million viewers and a presenter who interrupts. They want a
person who *lived it*. That is you now.

- *Say what you think* – you are quoted, clipped, and known.
- *Say what they want* – you are invited back. It pays.
- *Decline* – a quiet Thursday.
- *Let it ring* – they find someone else who lived it.
- *Someone else's story* – a woman from the call centre, in your words. People call the station.

cards.title: Jonas Weber
cards.name: Jonas Weber
cards.back:
Jonas asked to be taught, which almost nobody does any more. He is clever in a way that is going out of fashion:
he wants to know why the machine does what it does, not only that it does it. He will be very good in five years,
if there is still a job called engineer.

cards.title: The junior colleague

options.text: Yes. One hour a week.
Yes, and bring him into your team.
No. There is no time.
Say you will think about it.

cards.back:
He is twenty-seven, clever in a way that is going out of fashion, and he asks – directly, which is rare – whether
you would teach him what you know. He has already learned what the model knows.

- *One hour* – it costs you an hour and gives you someone who tells you what the young think.
- *Bring him in* – he is good with machines. Very.
- *No* – he asks someone else. You notice you said no.
- *Think about it* – he waits a while. Then he asks someone else.

cards.title: The paper lets half the desk go

options.text: Take the package and go freelance.
Stay, and write the story about your own paper.
Use the union list you built.
Wait.
Hire one of them yourself, for anything.

cards.back:
Twenty-two names on a list that was clearly sorted by something. The model writes the sports pages now, the
weather, the markets and, on quiet days, the editorial. The two seniors are on the list. One of them is not you.

- *The package* – you are free and alone. The money lasts a season.
- *Write it* – the best story you have ever had and the last one for that paper.
- *The union list* – you organised early. Now it means something.
- *Wait* – your salary is renegotiated downward.
- *Hire one* – a sub-editor who now proofreads your letters. Better than any model.

cards.title: The evening course

options.text: Finish it.
Use the model instead. It translates.
Take the course with a friend.

cards.back:
Forty evenings, a teacher who was a diplomat, a language your grandmother spoke. The model translates it
perfectly and you still cannot order bread in it.

- *Finish* – you can order bread. People in that country treat you differently. (In Prototype 1 there is no
  skill gain on a card; the concept lists it – the author gives the trait and the influence instead.)
- *The model* – it translates. You do not learn anything, which you notice later.
- *With a friend* – you learn half as much and laugh twice as often.

cards.title: Leo Brandt
cards.name: Leo Brandt
cards.back:
Leo fixes things that are not supposed to be fixable and breaks things that are not supposed to be breakable, in
that order, for whoever asked first. He has never had a contract longer than six months and has never been out of
work. He will tell you a model can do what he does. He will not tell you he is afraid of it.

cards.title: Leo stops answering

options.text: Find him.
Ask your friend in intelligence. He knows people who know.
Wait.
Report him missing. Keep calling.

cards.back:
Four days, no messages. His flat is tidy, which it never is. The last thing he traced was a server, and the server
belonged to a ministry, and the ministry belonged to a block that is not yours.

- *Find him* – you do. He is fine, and now the people who have him know your name.
- *Your friend in intelligence* – he makes a call. Leo turns up in six months with a story he will not tell.
- *Wait* – Leo does not come back.
- *Keep calling* – five months later, a message: I'm fine. Don't ask. Then he is back.

cards.title: Li Na
cards.name: Li Na
cards.back:
Li Na built antenna arrays for the state for twelve years, then for a company that was the state in a different
jacket. She reads the pattern as a drawing, because she reads everything as a drawing. She left Beijing in April
with two suitcases and a copy of the eleven days. She says it was for a conference.

cards.title: The wallet

options.text: Cancel everything. Start again.
It comes back in the post, with everything in it.
Ask the taxi company, politely.

cards.back:
A taxi, a pocket, gone. Cards, cash, the photo you do not admit you carry.

- *Cancel* – an afternoon of phone calls with models that are very sorry.
- *It comes back* – a stranger, a stamp, no note. You think about them for a week.
- *The taxi company* – a model answers, then a man named Rui, who finds it under a seat.

cards.title: Made by humans

options.text: Put the label on everything you make.
Sell the label. It is a market now.
Hang it in the gallery as the work itself.
Buy only things that carry it, for a month.
Notice it in shops.

cards.back:
A small blue label, a hand drawn in one line: made by humans. It started on cheese in the Jura. By spring it is on
furniture, bread, tax returns and one airline. It is worth eleven per cent more at the till. Nobody checks it.

- *Everything* – your housings carry a hand now. Customers pay for it, which surprises you.
- *Sell it* – you license it. Within a year it is on things a model made.
- *The gallery* – one label, framed, alone on a white wall. People queue.
- *A month* – things are more expensive and you like them more.
- *Notice* – you start looking for it without meaning to.

cards.title: Mara Lindqvist
cards.name: Mara Lindqvist
cards.back:
Mara owns a mid-sized factory near Łódź that makes the housings nobody notices – for pumps, for charging stations,
for whatever the year wants. She took it over from an uncle who thought she would sell. She did not. She is the
kind of person who reads the fine print at two in the morning and enjoys it. She has never lost money on purpose
and never told the whole truth when half of it would do.

If you play Mara, the Boom is a market first and a question later. Her factory is the thing that can make her rich
and the thing that can make her nobody.

cards.title: Marta Kowalska
cards.name: Marta Kowalska
cards.back:
Marta is the mayor of the town next to the factory, and of four thousand people who used to work in places like it.
She was a teacher, then a union rep, then the only candidate. She knows every family by its kitchen. She does not
like people from the capital, and she says so to their faces, which they find refreshing exactly once.

cards.title: Dr. Meera Iyer
cards.name: Meera Iyer
cards.back:
Meera runs a clinic in Chennai over video for villages that have a phone and no doctor. A model does the first
look; she does the second. She thinks Europe is having the wrong argument about the models – the question is not
who loses a job, but who never had a doctor in the first place.

cards.title: Moving house

options.text: Somewhere smaller, closer to people.
Somewhere bigger. You have earned it.
Stay. Paint the kitchen.

cards.back:
The landlord is selling. Or the stairs are getting long. Or the neighbourhood has turned into somewhere else. There
is a flat across town, and one further out, and the boxes in the cellar from the last time.

- *Smaller* – you give away two hundred books and find out which twenty you needed.
- *Bigger* – a room you do not know what to do with yet.
- *Stay* – a new colour, the same window. It is home again.

cards.title: Nadia Fall
cards.name: Nadia Fall
cards.back:
Nadia runs the 800 metres faster than anyone in Europe and slower than three women elsewhere. She is sponsored by
a shoe and a bank. She reads her own contracts, which her agent finds annoying. She is the one person in this set
whose job a model cannot do, and she knows it.

cards.title: The hedge

options.text: Cut it. Say sorry.
Let your lawyer write a letter.
Talk to him over the hedge.

cards.back:
Forty centimetres of hedge, thirty years of neighbours, one letter from a model that cites the relevant
ordinance. He is seventy-four. He is also right.

- *Cut it* – an hour on a Saturday and an invitation to a barbecue.
- *The letter* – you win. He does not speak to you again.
- *Over the hedge* – twenty minutes about his late wife, who planted it. You leave it as it is.

cards.title: Niklas Berg
cards.name: Niklas Berg
cards.back:
Niklas builds the things nobody sees: the sensors on a bridge, the cooling in a server hall, the receiver on a
dish. He speaks when he has something to say, which his colleagues took three years to understand and now rely
on. He wears a watch that was his grandfather's and a white T-shirt that is always the same one, as far as anyone
can tell. He notices what is wrong in a room before anyone else does and says so last. He has two offers on his
desk, one from a ministry and one from a company that is the ministry in a different jacket, and he has not
answered either.

If you play Niklas, you are the person who can read the drawing. That is worth more this year than it has ever
been, and more people know it than you would like.

cards.title: Ninety days under

options.text: Send your engineer. The navy pays well.
Send your engineer, and ask for the report.
Not your people. Not for that long.

cards.back:
The navy needs a civilian engineer aboard for a patrol: a new reactor control system, and the manufacturer's
people are not cleared. Ninety days, no signal, no mail. It pays like a year. Your engineer is the only person you
know who qualifies, and he would go.

- *Send him* – three months without him. The money arrives before he does.
- *The report* – he comes back with a story about what the models cannot run. It is worth more than the money.
- *Not your people* – he hears about it anyway. He is not sure whether to be grateful.

cards.title: Oil falls and keeps falling

options.text: Buy the cheap tankers and turn them into something.
Write what it means for the Gulf.
Fill the tank. Drive somewhere far.
Watch the number.

cards.back:
The models plan the routes, the routes are shorter, the lorries are electric, and the world needs eleven per cent
less oil than the year before. The price falls for nine months. In three countries in the Gulf, budgets written for
a hundred dollars a barrel meet a world that pays forty. Nobody in Europe notices, except at the pump.

- *Tankers* – forty ships for the price of one. Somebody will want them for something.
- *The Gulf* – you write the piece nobody else does: what happens to a country when the thing it sells ends.
- *Drive* – cheap petrol, an empty road, the last summer of it.
- *Watch* – the number goes down. Then it stops.

cards.title: Oskar Lind
cards.name: Oskar Lind
cards.back:
Oskar runs a parish outside Uppsala that has more funerals than baptisms, and a food bank that has more of both.
He believes the models are a test, not a tool. He is kind to everyone who disagrees with him and keeps a list of
them.

cards.title: Parliament debates the model levy

options.text: Testify for the levy.
Testify against it.
Brief Hanna with the numbers from the factory.
Wait.
Send the committee one honest page.
Ask a politician you know to put your question.

cards.back:
A tax of three per cent on every euro a model earns in Europe, paid into a fund for the people it replaces. The
committee hears forty witnesses in two weeks. The models write most of the testimony on both sides, which
everybody knows and nobody says.

- *For* – you are on record. The companies note it.
- *Against* – you are on record. The unions note it.
- *Brief Hanna* – you give her something true. She will remember who gave it.
- *Wait* – the vote comes anyway.
- *One honest page* – it is quoted in the final report, without your name.
- *A politician you know* – your question, her voice, on the record.

cards.title: The pension fund buys model stock

options.text: Write that the fund is betting pensions on a bubble.
Sell them yours at the top.
Wait.
Ask the fund, in writing, to explain.

cards.back:
The largest pension fund in the north puts four per cent of everything into the index that doubled. The press
release calls it *participation in the transformation*. Your mother's pension is in it. So is Yusuf's.

- *Write it* – you are right and unpopular, in that order.
- *Sell them yours* – a good price from people who cannot afford it.
- *Wait* – it is not your money. Yet.
- *Ask in writing* – the reply is eleven pages long and says nothing. You frame page six.

cards.title: Dr. Priya Raman
cards.name: Priya Raman
cards.back:
Priya left Bangalore for Grenoble, then Grenoble for a startup, then the startup for a bigger one. She builds the
part of the models that decides what to forget. She is the person in the room who already knows what the next
room will say. She wants to go back to India with something to show for it.

cards.title: Ray Delgado
cards.name: Ray Delgado
cards.back:
Ray flew cargo for twenty-six years – the night runs from the Gulf to Panama, Houston to Bogotá, the ones with
the containers nobody asks about. Then he flew the hurricane season, then he stopped flying and started owning: two
old freighters, a hangar on the coast, a share in a yard where the containers stack to the sky at sunset. He is
tanned the way people are when they stopped caring about it, laughs easily, pays his crews first and himself
last, and has never once told anyone what was in the boxes. He has a daughter in Seoul who calls on Sundays.

If you play Ray, the world comes to you by sea and by air, and you know who is moving what before the news does. A
freighter is a slow way to be in the middle of everything.

cards.title: Everyone wants your racks

options.text: Rent them out, all of them.
Keep a third for your own model.
Sell the farm while it is worth something.
Wait.

cards.back:
The cold store outside Tallinn has become the most sought-after address in the Baltics. Three companies will pay
anything for the racks by the end of the quarter. Anything, this year, is a lot.

- *Rent all* – the money is immediate. The contracts are short.
- *Keep a third* – you own something that thinks. Expensive, interesting.
- *Sell* – the best price you will ever see for a cold store.
- *Wait* – a little money comes in anyway.

cards.title: Dr. Rosa Almeida
cards.name: Rosa Almeida
cards.back:
Rosa runs the night shift on the plateau: eleven years of pulsars, calibration, thin air and instant coffee. She
was the one awake at 03:12. She has not told her mother. She does not want to be famous; she wants to be right,
and she wants whoever gets to speak for the pattern to have actually read it.

cards.title: Rosa comes to dinner

options.text: Cook. Do not talk about it until dessert.
Ask her the question you have not asked anyone: are you frightened?

cards.back:
She is in Europe for a week of meetings she hates. She brings wine from the valley below the plateau and a
photograph of the dish at dawn, and for two hours nobody says the word "signal".

- *Cook* – at dessert she says: "It is still there. Every eleven days. I check, every time, as if it might not be."
- *Are you frightened* – "No," she says. "I am frightened of us."

cards.title: Someone cuts the cables

options.text: Condemn it, clearly, in public.
Find out who they are and why.
Say you understand them.
Check that yours are safe.
Watch the news.

cards.back:
At three in the morning, in a field outside Frankfurt, someone cuts the fibre into Europe's second-largest data
centre with an angle grinder and leaves a note: "We were here first." The models are down for six hours across
the continent. A group nobody has heard of claims it. Their website is very well written.

- *Condemn* – it is the right thing. It sounds like the wrong side.
- *Who* – a former network engineer, a nurse, two students. None of them have records.
- *Understand* – you do. Saying it costs you.
- *Yours* – a security firm, a fence, a camera that watches the camera.
- *News* – six hours. Then everything again.

cards.title: Dr. Samir Haddad
cards.name: Samir Haddad
cards.back:
Samir runs the night shift in an emergency room in Marseille and a small telemedicine company in the daytime,
which is why he is always tired and never bored. He believes the models will save more lives than they cost. He
has seen both kinds of night. He is the person the nurses call when the machine says one thing and the patient
says another.

If you play Samir, the Boom is a question of who gets seen first – and who decides.

cards.title: Seoul
cards.name: Seoul
cards.back:
Ten million people who adopted everything first – the phones, the models, the robots that bring the coffee – and
are the first to find out what it costs. The chip fabs are an hour south. The parliament is arguing about a
four-day week. Outside the blocks, inside everyone's supply chain.

cards.title: The server farm
cards.name: The server farm
cards.back:
A former cold store outside Tallinn, four hundred racks, a power contract that was cheap in 2023. Whoever owns
compute in the Boom owns the thing everybody wants to rent. Whoever owns it in the Bust owns a cold store.

cards.title: Silence

options.text: Say it in public: a gap is data. Wait eleven days before you grieve.
Say it in public: a gap is data. Wait eleven days before you grieve.
Open your doors. The Watch has nowhere to go tonight.
Buy. Everything. The fear is pricing the end of the story; the story is not over.
Sit with it. Eleven days is a long time.

cards.back:
At 03:12 on the day it should come, it does not. Rosa checks the receiver, the clock, the sky. Nothing. For the
first time since January the world does not know what it is waiting for. The Watch's leader says it has left us.
The markets agree. Eleven days later it is back, exactly as before, as if nothing happened. Something happened.

- *A gap is data* – you said "wait". People remember who said wait on the night everyone said over.
- *Open your doors* – forty people in your front room, in silence, until morning.
- *Buy* – it comes back. So does the market. You were there a week early.
- *Sit with it* – eleven days of not knowing. Most people cannot. You can.

cards.title: Sofia Marin
cards.name: Sofia Marin
cards.back:
Sofia reads contracts the way other people read faces. She has a small practice in Lyon, two assistants, and the
quiet reputation of someone who has never lost a case she chose to take. She chooses carefully. In 2026 she gets
three calls a week from people who want to know whether a model's contract is a contract.

cards.title: The solar park
cards.name: The solar park
cards.back:
Forty hectares of panels on a former airbase in Brandenburg, sheep between the rows. It was a tax shelter. Then
every data centre in the north wanted power, and it became the kind of asset people call you about on Sundays.

cards.title: Someone answers

options.text: Point the array at the source and send the eleven days back.
Put Europe's name on the reply. You wrote half of it.
Put Europe's name on the reply. You wrote half of it.
Argue in every room you can reach that nobody should answer.
Let the blocks do what blocks do.

cards.back:
The committee has met eleven times and agreed on nothing. Then, on a Tuesday, a dish in the Gobi transmits for
nine hours. China says it was a test. Nobody believes China. By Friday the Americans have transmitted too, and
Europe is writing a statement about the importance of coordination.

- *Answer yourself* – a private array, a private reply. Legal in no country and done in all of them.
- *Europe's name* – the reply that is actually sent carries the lines you argued for. It is a small thing and
  everyone in the room knows it.
- *Nobody should answer* – you lose. But the people who agreed with you remember you as the one who said it.
- *Let them* – three replies are on their way. Whatever is out there now knows there are at least three of us.

cards.title: Everything that touches a model goes up

options.text: Buy in.
Sell what you have.
Ask your scientist friend which ones are real.
Wait.
Buy a little. Only what you can lose.
Ask a business contact for a tip.

cards.back:
The index that tracks companies with the word *model* in their filings doubles in six weeks. Your neighbour's
cousin has made more than you did last year. The people who understand the models say it cannot last. The people
who do not understand them say the same thing and buy anyway.

- *Buy in* – you will be right for a while.
- *Sell* – you take the money and the regret.
- *Ask your scientist friend* – she names three that will survive. One of them is hers.
- *Wait* – nothing happens to you, which is a choice.
- *A little* – you are in, a bit. It feels sensible, which may be the danger.
- *A business contact* – he says get out by summer. You make a little and remember the sentence.

cards.title: The one that paid off

options.text: Take the money out.
Let it ride.
Give a third of it away.
Do nothing. Look at the number.
Take half out.

cards.back:
The thing you bought in the spring is worth four times what you paid. Your banker, who is a model, suggests
holding. Your banker, who is a person, suggests lunch.

- *Take it out* – it is real money now.
- *Let it ride* – it goes up a little more. Then there is a Tuesday.
- *Give a third* – you are known for it.
- *Do nothing* – the number is nice to look at. Some of it stays.
- *Half* – half real, half a hope.

cards.title: The anniversary

options.text: The same restaurant as the first time.
Somewhere neither of you has been.
Forget it. Apologise for a week.

cards.back:
The date is in the calendar and in the model's reminder and somehow still comes as a surprise. There is a person
who has put up with this whole year. There should be a table, and a candle, and you without a phone.

- *The same restaurant* – the waiter is new and the soup is the same.
- *Somewhere new* – a train, a small town, a hotel with a creaking floor.
- *Forget* – the week of apologies is its own kind of anniversary.

cards.title: The answer committee

options.text: Take the chair. Write Europe's position yourself.
Sit on it. Argue for the open reply: say who we are, all of us.
Sit on it. Argue for silence until we know what it says.
Send a politician you know. Give her your notes.
Read the minutes when they leak.

cards.back:
Europe's committee on the reply meets in a building with a view of the sea and a mandate to decide whether, how
and in whose name to answer. Eleven members. Two have read the paper. One has read the eleven days.

- *The chair* – you are the person who decides what Europe says to the sky. The sentence is yours.
- *The open reply* – a list of everything we are. It is long and it is honest and half the room hates it.
- *Silence* – the quiet argument. You win the room and lose the world, which is answering anyway.
- *Your politician* – your notes are in her speech. Her name is in the minutes.
- *The minutes* – they leak on Thursday. You read them with everyone else.

cards.title: Ten weeks on the line

options.text: Do it. Learn the line from the people on it.
Do two weeks. Enough to know.
You own it. You do not need to work it.

cards.back:
Yusuf's idea, said half as a joke: ten weeks on the line, a shift like everyone else, before you decide anything
about the model. The ninety would see you at six in the morning. The world would run without you for a season.

- *Ten weeks* – you come back with hands that know the work. Nobody on the floor calls you by your surname again.
- *Two weeks* – a gesture. A good one. They know it was a gesture.
- *You own it* – true. It is the kind of true that costs.

cards.title: The array
cards.name: A share in the array
cards.back:
Twelve dishes on a plateau in the Atacama, run by a foundation that is always short of money and, since January,
never short of visitors. A share buys you a seat on its board, a key to the control room and eleven days of data
before anyone else sees them. It also buys you the bills.

cards.title: Someone wants to go home

options.text: Let them go, with thanks. Keep in touch.
Ask them to stay three more months.
Offer more money.

cards.back:
It is the one you sent away the most. Toronto, Seoul, the factory, the roof. They come back from the last one and
say, carefully, that they would like a year at home. Not a complaint. A request.

- *Let them go* – a contact now, a friend still. The team is one smaller and the story is one longer.
- *Three months* – they stay. They count the days, politely.
- *More money* – they take it. Something between you is now a transaction.

cards.title: The banker's reading

options.text: Look at the count the way you look at a balance sheet.
Ask the consortium's analysts. They have been counting since February.
Ask a businessperson you know what her analysts count.
A week with the numbers and a spreadsheet.
Leave the decoding to the blocks.

cards.back:
Daniel's people think the pattern is a tally. Not a message: a ledger. How many, how often, where. And they have
noticed that one number in the eleven days has gone up twice since the dish in the Gobi transmitted.

- *The balance sheet* – you see it. The number is a count, and the count has changed since we started talking.
- *The analysts* – they show you the chart. Then they ask you not to show anyone else.
- *Leave it* – the market reads it anyway. Markets always do.

cards.title: The blocks know

options.text: Brief your block before the others brief theirs.
Brief your block before the others brief theirs.
Ask a politician you know what the cabinet was told.
Buy antenna makers. Quietly.
Watch the five statements. They say the same thing in five ways.

cards.back:
Someone in the observatory's funding chain tells someone in a ministry. Within a week five governments know and
three of them have called it a hoax in public and a priority in private. China pulls its two dishes out of the
shared network. The United States asks for the raw data and gets a copy that is eleven days short.

- *Brief your block* – Europe hears it from you. That is remembered when the committee is formed.
- *Ask your politician* – the cabinet was told it is real and told not to say so.
- *Buy antenna makers* – everyone will want a dish. You own the people who make them.
- *Watch* – the blocks begin to sort themselves: those who want to hear more and those who want it to stop.

cards.title: The book comes out

options.text: Do the tour. Twelve cities, one suitcase.
Sign in one bookshop and go home.

cards.back:
It is in every airport. The cover has a dish on it that is not yours. Chapter nine is the one people quote.

- *The tour* – you are tired and recognised and paid. All three at once.
- *One bookshop* – the money comes anyway. Less of it, and you sleep in your own bed.

cards.title: The book offer

options.text: Sign. Advance now, the rest when it is out.
Sign. Advance now, the rest when it is out.
Sign. Advance now, the rest when it is out.
Say no. You have a day job.

cards.back:
An editor in London, a deadline in autumn, a title you hate: "Eleven Days". She wants the inside of the year from
someone who was inside it. The advance is small; the rest is not.

- *Sign* – evenings and weekends for a season. In autumn, a book with your name on it, in every airport.
- *Say no* – somebody else writes it. Worse.

cards.title: The book

options.text: Finish it.
Ask the model what happens.
Read it aloud to someone.

cards.back:
Four hundred pages, a bookmark at 180 since March. It is good. It is slow. Everyone you know has read the summary.

- *Finish it* – the last hundred pages are the reason it was written.
- *The summary* – accurate. Nothing in it stays with you.
- *Aloud* – a chapter a night. It takes all winter. Neither of you minds.

cards.title: The briefing

options.text: Brief the cabinet. Say what is known and stop there.
Brief the cabinet. Say what is known and stop there.
Brief them and ask for the chair of the committee that does not exist yet.
Send a politician you know in your place.
Decline. You do not brief governments.

cards.back:
A room in Brussels with no windows, fourteen ministers and a projector that does not work. They have the five
statements, a translation of the Chinese one and no idea what the pattern is. They have been told you do.

- *Say what is known* – twenty minutes, no adjectives. They have never heard anyone do that. They remember.
- *Ask for the chair* – there will be a committee by June. You are on it, or you run it.
- *Send your politician* – she does well. It is her name they remember.
- *Decline* – a man from a think tank briefs them instead. He uses the word "paradigm".

cards.title: Someone asks whether it is a bubble

options.text: Say yes, on television.
Say no, and mean it.
Say it depends, and explain on what.
Wait.
Answer with a story from your own year.

cards.back:
It is asked on a Sunday evening programme by a presenter who wants a yes or a no. Everyone who says yes has been
wrong for eighteen months. Everyone who says no has been right and is rich. You are asked.

- *Yes* – you lose a little money and gain a sentence people will quote later.
- *No* – the market agrees with you, for now.
- *It depends* – nobody quotes it. It is the only true answer.
- *Wait* – someone else answers.
- *Your own year* – not yes or no. A story. It is the clip that travels.

cards.title: Someone was in the flat

options.text: Change the locks, add a camera.
Find out who. You have ways.
Let it go. It was only things.

cards.back:
The door is fine. The window is not. A laptop, a watch from your father, the spare cash in the tea tin. The police
officer is kind and types the report into a model that says the case has a four per cent chance.

- *Locks* – you sleep better. You check the camera at night, which is not sleeping.
- *Who* – a seventeen-year-old two streets away. You get the watch back and do not press charges.
- *Let it go* – the watch is the only thing you miss. You miss it for years.

cards.title: The calibration fault

options.text: Pull the thread. Who signed the press line, and when.
Ask a hacker to look at the observatory's logs.
Ask your hacker to look at the observatory's logs.
Believe the press office. Most people do.

cards.back:
"A calibration fault affecting one receiver has been resolved." Fourteen words, no author, released on a Sunday.
The observatory's site has had four times its usual traffic since. Somebody in Chile is working very hard to
make nothing look like nothing.

- *Pull the thread* – the line was signed by the director and dictated by a ministry. Now you know what they know.
- *The logs* – 03:12, every eleven days. It is in the machine, whatever the press office says.
- *Believe them* – you find out in June with everyone else.

cards.title: The call centre closes

options.text: Hire twenty of them, for anything.
Help Marta keep the building for the town.
Run their stories in the paper.
Give to the fund for the families.
It was coming.

cards.back:
Four hundred people answered the phone for a bank, an airline and a telecom company. On the first of the month the
model answered instead, and nobody calling noticed. The building is on the edge of town, next to the bus station.
Marta, the mayor, stands in front of it with a microphone and no plan.

- *Hire twenty* – twenty is not four hundred. To twenty families it is everything.
- *The building* – the town gets a hall. What goes in it is the next question.
- *The paper* – four hundred names in eleven thousand homes.
- *The fund* – your money, quietly.
- *It was coming* – it was. That does not help.

cards.title: The car dies

options.text: Buy a new one.
Do without. Trains, feet, favours.
Borrow one.

cards.back:
On the motorway, in the rain, with a meeting at nine. The tow truck driver is a person. You tip him more than
you meant to.

- *New car* – a problem solved with money, which is what money is for.
- *Do without* – you ask for lifts. People like being asked.
- *Borrow one* – someone lends you theirs. You owe them now.

cards.title: The gala

options.text: Go, and give.
Go, and work the room.
Send a cheque. Stay home.
Do not go.

cards.back:
Black tie, a ballroom, a fund for the people the models replaced, run by the people who replaced them. The food
is excellent. Hanna is at table four.

- *Give* – you are seen giving.
