- *Work the room* – you leave with four names and a promise.
- *A cheque* – it does the same good and nobody sees it.
- *Do not go* – nobody notices. Hanna does.

cards.title: The check-up

options.text: Do what the doctor says. All of it.
Ask your doctor what really matters.
Walk to work for a month.
Nod. Change nothing.
Ask a doctor you know what really matters.

cards.back:
Nothing wrong. Nothing right either: the numbers are all a little higher than last time, the way the year was a
little heavier. The doctor reads the model's summary aloud and then puts it down and says, in her own words: slow
down.

- *All of it* – less coffee, more walking, earlier nights. It is boring. It works.
- *Your doctor* – she says three things matter and the rest is noise. You can do three things.
- *Walk* – forty minutes each way. You start noticing the trees on the route.
- *Nod* – the next check-up is in a year. You will think about it then.
- *A doctor you know* – over dinner, not in the surgery. Two things. You do one of them.

cards.title: The chip embargo

options.text: Ask Viktor what the chips can really do.
Buy what is left before the price moves.
Back Europe building its own fab.
Write to your member of parliament.
It is far away.

cards.back:
Washington forbids the export of the newest chips to China; Beijing forbids the export of the metals the chips are
made of. Europe, which makes the machines that make the chips, is asked by both sides which side it is on. The
answer, by Friday, is "a working group".

- *Viktor* – he explains, over a bad line from Tbilisi, why the numbers in the papers are wrong.
- *Buy* – you own something scarce. Scarce things get noticed.
- *A fab* – ten billion euros and seven years. Someone has to say yes first.
- *Write* – you get a reply, signed by a model on the member's behalf.
- *Far away* – it does not stay far away.

cards.title: The racks are empty

options.text: Offer it to Aisha's lab for nothing.
Run your own model on it, now that compute is cheap.
Sell it as a cold store.
Lend it to the town as a winter shelter.

cards.back:
The three companies that would pay anything have paid nothing since Tuesday. Four hundred racks, a power
contract, and silence. It is, again, a building outside Tallinn that is cold.

- *Give it away* – the lab does something with it that nobody will sell.
- *Your own model* – cheap compute, no customers, a strange freedom.
- *Sell* – it was always a cold store.
- *A shelter* – four hundred racks out, two hundred beds in. Marta cuts a ribbon.

cards.title: The consortium's offer

options.text: Sell him the eleven days. Cash, today.
Take his money as a partner, not a seller.
Take the meeting. Take nothing else.
Do not answer the email.

cards.back:
Daniel Ross has a consortium, a jet and a theory: whoever owns the data owns the market, and the market is the
sky. He wants the raw files, or your name on his board, or at least an hour. He pays for the hour either way.

- *Sell* – three months of money for eleven days of numbers. Rosa will find out.
- *Partner* – less money now, a share of what comes. Daniel keeps his word about money.
- *The meeting* – a man who knows everyone now knows you.
- *Do not answer* – he buys the data from someone else.

cards.title: The consultancy

options.text: Advise the consortium. Two days a month, a fee that is not small.
Advise a block. They pay less and ask more.
Advise anyone who asks. You have had a year of it.
Advise anyone who asks. You have had a year of it.
Advise the Watch. For nothing.
Nobody needs another consultant.

cards.back:
A year ago nobody knew what you knew. Now everyone wants to pay for it: the consortium, two ministries, a bank, a
film studio, a movement in a field. The work is the same – saying what is known and stopping there – and the
fee, for once, is not.

- *The consortium* – Daniel pays on the first of the month. He always has.
- *A block* – a smaller fee and a seat closer to the table.
- *Anyone* – it is honest work and it pays.
- *The Watch* – they cannot pay. They listen, which is rarer.

cards.title: The count goes up

options.text: Say it plainly: we do not know what is counted. Stop guessing in public.
Short everything the fear is selling.
Go to the plateau. Sit with Rosa and the number.
Watch the number with everyone else.

cards.back:
Since the Gobi transmitted, the one number everyone now calls the count has gone up three times. Since the
Americans transmitted, twice more. Nobody has said what it counts. Everybody has decided.

- *Say it plainly* – it is the least satisfying thing anyone has said all year. It is also the only true one.
- *Short the fear* – the fear is overpriced. You were right by Friday.
- *The plateau* – Rosa shows you the number. "It went up when we talked," she says. "That is all we know."
- *Watch* – the markets fall, the generals rise. The count does not care.

cards.title: Something has to be carried by hand

options.text: Send your spy. It is his kind of errand.
Send your pilot. He asks no questions.
Go yourself. Know what you are carrying.
Decline. You are not a courier.

cards.back:
A drive, the size of a thumb, that cannot go over any network: the weights of something, or the evidence of
something, or both. It has to be in Bangalore in two weeks, in a hand that was in Europe when it left. The people
asking pay well and explain nothing.

- *Your spy* – he is back in two weeks with a tan and no comment.
- *Your pilot* – he flies it himself, in a plane with no transponder. Legal, he says. Mostly.
- *Yourself* – you open the drive on the plane. You wish you had not.
- *Decline* – someone else carries it. You read about it in the spring.

cards.title: The minister said something she did not say

options.text: Prove it is fake, fast, in public.
Have your hacker trace where it came from.
Say nothing. Watch what it does to the levy.
Wait.
Share the correction, not the video.
Ask a hacker you know to check the file.

cards.back:
Forty seconds of video: the minister for digital affairs, in her own voice, calling the levy a mistake and the
unemployed lazy. It is perfect. It is false. By the time that is established, eleven million people have watched
it and the committee has postponed the vote.

- *Prove it* – you are the person who was right first. She knows your name now.
- *Your hacker* – he finds the server. The server finds him.
- *Say nothing* – the lie does your work for you. You notice that you let it.
- *Wait* – Europe trusts a little less.
- *The correction* – it travels a tenth as far. It is the tenth that matters.
- *A hacker you know* – the file has a fingerprint. You send it to the minister's office.

cards.title: The dish in the Gobi

options.text: Publish what your spy told you: it is a transmitter, and it is finished.
Ask the engineer who built arrays for Beijing what it can do.
Point your own array at the Gobi. If they transmit, you will hear it first.
Watch the satellite picture on the news: a circle in the sand.

cards.back:
A satellite photo, two hundred metres of dish in a desert that had nothing in it in March. China says it is a
receiver. Receivers do not need a cooling plant the size of a town. The committee adjourns. The market drops.
Everybody who argued for silence has lost the argument without a word being sent.

- *Publish* – the world learns on a Tuesday that someone is about to answer. Your name is on the story.
- *Ask Li Na* – "It can send. It is meant to. And they will."
- *Point your array* – you will know within the hour. Knowing within the hour is what the array is for.
- *The news* – a circle in the sand, a voice-over, a general. Fear is on sale and everyone buys.

cards.title: The auction

options.text: Auction the August nights to the highest block.
Auction them, but keep the eleven days for Rosa.
Give August to the open network. Everyone sees everything.
Keep the nights. The bills can wait a month.

cards.back:
Three blocks and the consortium want August. The board wants the roof fixed. Rosa wants the nights the pattern
arrives. The foundation's lawyer has written the word "auction" on a whiteboard and underlined it twice.

- *Highest block* – the roof, the road and a year of coffee. The block puts a soldier in the control room.
- *Keep the eleven days* – a little less money, and Rosa still sees it first.
- *Open network* – the plateau becomes the one place everyone trusts. That is worth more than August.
- *Wait* – the roof leaks. Rosa does not notice. The accountant does.

cards.title: Dish time

options.text: Rent the nights to a block. They pay by the hour.
Rent the nights to the consortium. He pays more and asks less.
Keep the nights. Point it where Rosa says.

cards.back:
Twelve dishes, three hundred and sixty-five nights, and everyone on earth wants an hour. The board meets by video
and looks at you. The bills are on the table; so are the offers.

- *A block* – steady money, and a ministry that thinks it owns your calendar.
- *The consortium* – better money, and Daniel's name on the data you collect.
- *Keep them* – Rosa points it at the source every night. You pay for that. You also see things first.

cards.title: The doctor's reading

options.text: Two weeks with the numbers. They are not a shape. They are a sequence.
Ask a doctor you know to look at the repeat. It is a protein, she thinks.
Give the repeat to your doctor. She goes quiet for a week.
Two weeks with the numbers and a biology textbook.
Leave the decoding to the blocks.

cards.back:
A doctor in your life has looked at the repeat and gone quiet. The three clicks, she says, are not clicks; they
are a sequence, and sequences in threes are how life writes things down. If it is a sequence, it is a sequence
for something. If it is for something, someone is telling us to avoid it.

- *Two weeks* – you come out the other side certain it is a warning and unable to say of what.
- *Your doctor* – "I would not build it. Whatever it is."
- *Leave it* – the generals decode it. They do not tell anyone either.

cards.title: The documentary

options.text: Give them two weeks and your face.
Give them two weeks and your face.
Give them two weeks and your face.
Advise, off camera, for a fee.
No cameras.

cards.back:
A crew from a streaming service, a director who has made two good films and one bad one, a budget that would run
the plateau for a year. They want the year of the signal from someone who lived it. Two weeks, your kitchen,
your face.

- *Two weeks* – the film is good. Strangers in airports know your kitchen.
- *Off camera* – the fee is smaller and so is everything else.
- *No cameras* – the film is made without you, and about you.

cards.title: The dog

options.text: Keep him.
Find him a home.

cards.back:
He was outside the factory for three days, or the gallery, or the lab, depending on who you are. Medium-sized,
polite, no collar. He has decided.

- *Keep him* – walks, twice a day, in all weather. You talk to him about the Boom.
- *A home* – Yusuf's daughter. She names him after a footballer.

cards.title: The new car

options.text: Electric, and a wallbox at home.
Used, cheap, whatever runs.
Share one with the neighbours.
No car. Bicycle and trains.

cards.back:
The old one failed its inspection with a list longer than the car. The dealer has a model that tells you which
car you want. It is not wrong, which is annoying.

- *Electric* – silent mornings, a cable in the drive, a strange pride at the first full charge.
- *Used* – it rattles. It is yours. It will run for ten years out of spite.
- *Share* – a spreadsheet on the fridge of the house next door. It works better than anyone thought.
- *Bicycle* – you are wetter and calmer.

cards.title: The engineer's reading

options.text: Two weeks with the numbers and a drawing board. It is a shape.
Give the numbers to the engineer who left Beijing. She has already started.
Ask an engineer you know to read it as a drawing.
Two weeks with the numbers, no training, a lot of paper.
Leave the decoding to the blocks.

cards.back:
The pattern is numbers. The engineers in your life have started to see dimensions in them: a ratio that is a
circle, a repeat that is a material, a count that is a tolerance. Li Na says it is a ring and that she could
build it. Nobody has asked her to.

- *Two weeks* – at the end there is a drawing on your wall and you cannot stop looking at it.
- *Give it to her* – she comes back with the drawing in three days. She has not slept.
- *Leave it* – the blocks decode it too. Later, and they do not tell you.

cards.title: The roof came in

options.text: Go and fix it with the neighbours.
Send your pilot. He is handy and bored.
Pay a firm. Stay where you are.
Tarpaulin. Deal with it in spring.

cards.back:
The barn roof, under a metre of wet snow. Eleven hectares, no signal, and a building that is now open to the sky.
Two weeks of work for anyone who goes.

- *Yourself* – two weeks of hammering with people who have known the house longer than you.
- *Your pilot* – he enjoys it more than flying, he says.
- *A firm* – it costs. It is done. You were not there.
- *Tarpaulin* – it holds, mostly. Spring is a long way off.

cards.title: The line stopped

options.text: Go yourself. Stand on the floor until it runs.
Send your engineer. He fixes lines.
Phone the vendor. Wait for the patch.

cards.back:
Tuesday, 06:40: the model that runs the line has stopped scheduling and nobody knows why. Ninety people are
standing in a hall with their hands in their pockets. Every hour costs. Somebody has to be there.

- *Yourself* – a week in a hall in Poland. The line runs by Thursday. The ninety saw you.
- *Your engineer* – two days. He does not say what it was. It does not happen again.
- *The vendor* – a patch on Friday. A week of wages for nothing.

cards.title: The family dinner

options.text: Argue with your uncle about the models.
Change the subject to the food.
Listen to the youngest at the table.

cards.back:
Eleven people, one roast, a cousin who works in a data centre and an uncle who thinks the models are a plot. By the
dessert the table has split into those who are afraid and those who are not yet. Your grandmother asks for the salt.

- *Argue* – you win on points and lose the evening.
- *The food* – it was very good. Everyone agrees on that.
- *The youngest* – she is fourteen and has the clearest view at the table. Nobody else is listening to her.

cards.title: The tractors come to Brussels

options.text: Walk with them for a day.
Broker a meeting between them and the committee.
Explain why the model is right about the fields.
Avoid the centre that week.

cards.back:
The subsidy model has redrawn the map of what should grow where, and it is right, and a quarter of the farms in
Europe are on the wrong side of the line. Four thousand tractors on the ring road. Manure on the steps of the
Berlaymont. A seventy-year-old from Picardy on every front page, holding a sign that says: Ask me, not it.

- *Walk* – twelve kilometres, a sandwich from a stranger, sore feet.
- *Broker* – they meet. Nothing is agreed. Everyone says it went well.
- *Explain* – you are right. Being right in front of four thousand tractors is a skill you do not have.
- *Avoid* – the trams are cancelled anyway.

cards.title: The first component

options.text: Build the first segment on the plateau. Three weeks. See if the numbers were right.
Sell the drawings to the consortium. Let them build it.
Lock the drawings in a drawer.

cards.back:
A segment of the ring, four metres of it, built to the pattern's dimensions out of the pattern's material – which
turns out to be something a foundry in Ostrava can make. Nobody knows what a segment does. Everybody wants to see
one.

- *Build it* – it fits. Every measurement. That is the moment the world stops arguing whether and starts
  arguing who.
- *Sell the drawings* – the consortium builds it in a month and puts a fence around it.
- *The drawer* – someone else builds it. In the Gobi.

cards.title: The first hoax

options.text: Take it apart in public before the evening news runs it.
Ask your hacker where the file came from.
Check it against the real thing. You have the real thing.
Share it. Everybody is.

cards.back:
A second signal, from a second source, fourteen days long, and it decodes – the file says – to a face. It is on
every screen by noon. It is a fake, built in a weekend by someone with a good ear and a better sense of what
people want. Half the world believes it. The other half believes the first one was fake too.

- *Take it apart* – you show the seams. Tonight you are the person who said no.
- *Your hacker* – a studio in Tallinn, a client in a block that would like the world to stop listening.
- *The real thing* – you lay them side by side on the screen. The fake has a heartbeat. The real one does not.
- *Share it* – the morning after, your name is in the list of people who did.

cards.title: A company names a model as its CEO

options.text: Buy shares. If it works, it works.
Ask your lawyer whether it is legal.
Say on air what a CEO is for.
Laugh, and send it to a friend.
Ignore it.
Ask a lawyer you know whether it is legal.

cards.back:
A logistics firm in Rotterdam, two thousand employees, announces that its new chief executive is a model. A
human chair signs what the law requires a human to sign. The press release has a photograph of an empty chair.
The share price rises nine per cent before lunch.

- *Buy* – you will know in four months whether you were early or a fool.
- *Your lawyer* – she finds the paragraph that says a company must be led by a person. It is ambiguous.
- *On air* – you say a CEO is the person who is blamed. The clip travels.
- *Laugh* – it is funny, until it is not.
- *Ignore* – the chair stays empty.
- *A lawyer you know* – she finds the paragraph. It is ambiguous. So is she.

cards.title: The first snow

options.text: Go out in it. Now. In slippers.
Clear the pavement for the whole street.
Close the curtains.

cards.back:
It starts at dusk and nobody predicted it, not even the model. By nine the street is white and silent, the way it
was when you were seven. A neighbour you have never spoken to is standing in the middle of the road, laughing.

- *Slippers* – wet feet, cold hands, the best ten minutes of the winter.
- *The pavement* – six houses, one shovel, and on Monday three people say hello who did not before.
- *Curtains* – it is beautiful through the window too.

cards.title: The flu

options.text: Stay in bed.
Ask your doctor, and do what she says.
Work from bed.

cards.back:
A week in bed in the middle of everything. The model does not get the flu, which you think about at three in
the morning.

- *Bed* – a week lost. It costs a little.
- *Your doctor* – three days. She was right, as usual.
- *From bed* – you get things done and get better slower.

cards.title: The funding round

options.text: Sell half your stake at the round. The consortium is worth a country.
Hold. Whatever the ring is, it will be worth more when it opens.
Sell everything. You have seen what the count does.

cards.back:
Daniel's consortium raises more money in a morning than the plateau has cost in forty years. You were in early.
Daniel, who is never right about people, is right about this: the paper on the table is your share, and it is
worth what you want it to be.

- *Sell half* – you are richer than you have ever been and still in the room.
- *Hold* – the ring opens in a year or two. The share is a ticket.
- *Sell all* – the count has gone up again. You do not want to be counted.

cards.title: Will you be the godparent?

options.text: Yes, and mean it.
Yes, and send presents.
Say you are not the right person.
Ask for time.

cards.back:
Your oldest friend, in a café, holding a baby who is asleep in a way that looks permanent. She asks without
looking up. It means: if anything happens. It means: be someone this child can call.

- *Mean it* – birthdays, a zoo, later a phone call at two in the morning you will be glad to take.
- *Presents* – they arrive on time. The child likes you in the way children like the post.
- *Not the right person* – she is hurt, then grateful. She asks someone better.
- *Time* – she says of course. She does not ask again.

cards.title: The grant

options.text: Apply. 'Transient radio phenomena.' Do not say which one.
Apply with your block's name on it.
Send your scientist to stand in front of the panel.
Apply anyway. You have read the paper twice.
Skip it. Grants are paperwork.

cards.back:
Every science ministry on earth has discovered a sudden interest in radio astronomy. The money is real, the forms
are long and the panel sits in a week. Somebody has to go and stand in front of it.

- *Apply* – a year's funding for your dish time, your travel, your coffee. The panel does not ask what you
  are listening for. They know.
- *With the block's name* – the money comes faster, and so does the obligation.
- *Skip it* – the money goes to someone who filled in the form.

cards.title: The hearing on the Hill

options.text: Testify. Under oath, in plain words.
Testify. Under oath, in plain words.
Sit behind the man who testifies and write what he gets wrong.
Brief a lawyer you know on what the senators should ask.
Watch it on the evening news like everybody else.

cards.back:
Washington wants to know who knew what, when, and why a Chilean observatory on American money told the Americans
last. Four hours, nine senators, one of whom has read the paper. The room is full.

- *Testify* – you say "we do not know" eleven times. It is the most quoted testimony of the year.
- *Behind him* – the director gets three things wrong. Your piece runs at midnight.
- *Your lawyer* – the senator asks the one question that matters: who has the transmitter.
- *Evening news* – four hours cut to forty seconds. You get the forty seconds.

cards.title: The hearing

options.text: Tell the committee everything you know.
Protect your source, whatever they ask.
Bring your lawyer. Say only what she clears.
Ask for a closed session.

cards.back:
Room 4Q2, nine members, a camera, a glass of water. The model company sends its chief scientist, who is very
calm. You are sworn in after him. The chair asks you, politely, how you know what you know.

- *Everything* – you answer every question. It takes four hours. It is on every channel.
- *Your source* – you do not say her name. They threaten you with contempt. You hold.
- *Your lawyer* – careful, correct, a little dull. Nothing you said can be used.
- *Closed session* – no camera, more truth. The minutes are published in thirty years.

cards.title: The number one is not a person

options.text: Ask your artist friend to answer it with a live show.
Sing along. It is good.
Find the person who wrote the prompt.
Change the station.

cards.back:
For six weeks the most played song in Europe is sung by a voice that does not exist, about a summer nobody had. It
is very good. Children know all the words. A musician in Glasgow says it is the first song in history with no one
to thank, and that turns out to be wrong: a seventeen-year-old in Lyon typed the idea.

- *A live show* – a cellar in Berlin, three hundred people, a band that sweats. Nobody films it, for once.
- *Sing along* – it is catchy. You are allowed to like it.
- *The prompt* – she is shy and very surprised and owns nothing.
- *Change the station* – it is on that one too.

cards.title: The month everyone followed you

options.text: Use it. Sell something.
Use it. Say something.
Log off.
Keep posting and see what happens.
Use it. Point them at someone else.

cards.back:
One post, one night, three hundred thousand people. For a month you are the person they listen to about the
thing that happened to all of them. It will not last. That is the point of it.

- *Sell* – the month pays for itself and then some.
- *Say* – you spend it on something that is not you.
- *Log off* – the quiet is immediate and complete.
- *Keep posting* – it fades in a month, like it was always going to.
- *Someone else* – a food bank, a small band, a junior who lost her job. They get the month.

cards.title: A relative you barely knew

options.text: Take the house in the hills.
Take the money.
Take the airfield nobody wants.
Give it all to her village.

cards.back:
A lawyer's letter, a name you had to look up, a funeral with nine people. She left you a choice, which is the
most she could have left anyone: the house, the money, or the strip of grass with the hangar.

- *The house* – eleven hectares and no signal. It costs money and gives something else.
- *The money* – clean, simple, gone by autumn.
- *The airfield* – nobody wants it. One day it is the only way to be somewhere first.
- *Her village* – a plaque by the church with her name on it. Not yours.

cards.title: The insurer's model says no

options.text: Appeal, with every document you have.
Let your lawyer write one letter.
Find the clause and make it a story.
Phone them and ask for a person.
Pay it yourself.
Ask a lawyer you know for one sentence.

cards.back:
The water pipe in the cellar, the claim, four photographs, the reply in nine seconds: rejected, "pre-existing
condition of the property". There is no name at the bottom. There is a link to a satisfaction survey.

- *Appeal* – forty pages, three weeks, and then, without explanation, yes.
- *Your lawyer* – one page. Yes by return.
- *The clause* – thirty thousand other people had the same nine-second answer.
- *A person* – after an hour of music, a woman in Porto who says: let me see what I can do.
- *Pay* – it is quicker. It is not cheaper.
- *A lawyer you know* – one sentence, in your own email. They pay half.

cards.title: The last eleven days

options.text: Go to the plateau for the last cycle of the year. Stand in the control room at 03:12.
Listen at home, at 03:12, with the window open.
Sleep through it. It will come again in eleven days.

cards.back:
It has come thirty-three times this year, missing once. In January four people knew. Now there is a ring in the
desert, a committee with a view of the sea, a movement in a field and a count that nobody can read. And at 03:12
on the thirtieth of December the dish turns, and it is there.

- *The control room* – Rosa, the coffee, the screen. The line comes up. Nobody says anything. There is nothing
  to say that has not been said this year. That is the gift.
- *The window* – you cannot hear it. You listen anyway.
- *Sleep* – the most human thing anyone has done about it all year.

cards.title: The last junior

options.text: Take her on. Teach her the parts the model cannot do.
Tell her the truth and give her a name to call.
Wait.
Buy her lunch and listen.

cards.back:
She is twenty-four, has two degrees, and has just been told that the job she trained for is now a prompt. She
asks you, because you are the only person she knows who still has the job. She does not cry. That is worse.

- *Take her on* – it costs you a salary and gives you someone who will remember it.
- *Tell her the truth* – she goes to the name you gave her. The name owes you one.
- *Wait* – you did not say anything, and you notice that about yourself.
- *Lunch* – an hour. She leaves with a plan. You leave with her number.

cards.title: The leak is traced

options.text: Own it. You told the world because the world had a right to know.
Let a lawyer you know take the call.
Let your lawyer take the call.
Say nothing. Let them prove it.

cards.back:
The journalist you trusted protected her source. Her phone did not. A committee in Brussels has your name and
the date, and a journalist who did not get the story has both as well.

- *Own it* – a day of headlines, a week of letters, half of them grateful. You are the one who told us.
- *Your lawyer* – it goes away. Slowly, and at a price.
- *Nothing* – they cannot prove it. They do not need to.

cards.title: The lecture

options.text: Take the fee. Tell them what you know.
Take the fee. Tell them what everyone knows, well.
Take the fee. Tell them what everyone knows, well.
Waive the fee for a hall full of students.
Decline. You are not a speaker.

cards.back:
A university, a bank, a festival – everyone wants an evening about the eleven days and nobody who actually knows
anything will speak. You are on three lists. The fee is what a month costs.

- *What you know* – they came for this. They remember who told them.
- *What everyone knows, well* – the fee is the same; the applause is shorter.
- *Waive it* – two hundred students, one of whom will build something because of tonight.
- *Decline* – the fee goes to the man with the slides about Mars.

cards.title: The letter you never sent

options.text: Send it now.
Rewrite it, kinder.
Burn it in the garden.

cards.back:
In a drawer, under the warranty for a kettle you no longer have: a letter you wrote eight years ago to someone you
had a falling-out with and never sent. Your handwriting was angrier then. Most of it is still true.

- *Send it* – a reply comes in a week. Shorter than yours. Enough.
- *Kinder* – you write it again. This one you send. This one gets an answer.
- *Burn it* – a small fire, a glass of wine. Some things are finished by not being said.

cards.title: The levy comes to a vote

options.text: Call in what Hanna owes you.
Stand with the side you chose.
Stand with the side you chose.
Wait.
Phone your MEP the night before.
Ask a politician you know how it will go.

cards.back:
The vote is on a Wednesday. The lobbyist has been in every office. The strike is three weeks old. The deepfake is
still the second result when you search the minister's name. It passes or it fails by eleven votes, and which
depends on what you did in spring.

- *Call in Hanna* – it passes. The money for the fund comes from somewhere, and somewhere notices.
- *Your side, for* – Europe chooses its people over its numbers.
- *Your side, against* – Europe chooses its numbers over its people.
- *Wait* – without you, it fails.
- *Phone your MEP* – one call among four thousand. Eleven votes is not many.
- *A politician you know* – she tells you eleven votes. She is right to the vote.

cards.title: The bank's model wants a word

options.text: Show it the numbers it did not ask for.
Change banks. Today.
Call the branch manager you have known for years.
Accept the new rate.

cards.back:
Your credit line is "under review". The model has noticed that people in your postcode, with your kind of work,
in this year, default more often than they used to. It is not about you. It is about everyone like you, which turns
out to be the same thing.

- *Numbers* – you upload four years of accounts. The model apologises, in its way.
- *Change banks* – the other bank uses the same model. The rate is a little better.
- *The manager* – he is still there, two floors up, without a desk. He makes a call.
- *Accept* – a little more every month.

cards.title: The lobbyist calls

options.text: Take the meeting. Hear the number.
Take the meeting. Bring your politician friend.
Decline, and say so publicly.
Wait.
Take the meeting. Say nothing. Listen.

cards.back:
He represents four of the companies whose models are eating the continent, and he would like fifteen minutes of
your time about the levy. He is charming, well-briefed, and knows what you earn. The fifteen minutes come with a
consulting arrangement.

- *Hear the number* – it is a good number. People find out.
- *Bring your politician friend* – you are now the person who introduced the lobbyist to the committee chair. Useful. Remembered.
- *Decline publicly* – a small, clean, expensive thing to do.
- *Wait* – he calls someone else.
- *Listen* – you learn who else he has seen. He learns nothing about you.

cards.title: The local paper
cards.name: The local paper
cards.back:
A weekly, eleven thousand copies, a printing press older than the editor. It covers council meetings, football
and funerals, which is to say everything that matters to the people who read it. It loses a little money every
year. In the Boom it may be the last thing in the region a model did not write.

cards.title: Eight hundred kilometres

options.text: Walk all of it. Five weeks.
Walk one week of it.
Buy the boots. Leave them in the box.

cards.back:
The way to Santiago, from the Pyrenees, with a backpack under seven kilos and no plan beyond the next village. A
friend did it last year and came back with nothing to say except that you should do it. You have the boots. You
have the five weeks, if you take them.

- *All of it* – it costs you a month of cards. You come back a slightly different person, which was the point.
- *One week* – blisters, bread, a Danish couple you will write to for years.
- *In the box* – the boots look very good in the box.

cards.title: The man from the ministry

options.text: Give him the files and your reading of them. Ask for nothing.
Give him the files. Name your price.
Tell him you have nothing he does not.
Tell him the truth: you kept it because nobody asked.

cards.back:
He is polite, he has a lanyard, and he knows that you have had the eleven days since February and told nobody.
He would like them now. He would also like to know why.

- *Give them, ask nothing* – he writes down that you are a person who can be relied on. In Brussels that is a
  career.
- *Name your price* – he pays. He also writes down that you have a price.
- *Nothing he does not have* – if he believes you, you keep your month. If he does not, you are on a list.
- *The truth* – he does not understand it. He writes it down anyway.

cards.title: The marathon

options.text: Train with Nadia. Finish under four hours.
Run it for charity, slowly.
Stand at kilometre thirty with oranges.

cards.back:
Forty-two kilometres through a city you think you know. The registration closes on Friday. You have not run more
than ten since you were thirty. Everybody who has done it says the same thing about kilometre thirty, and nobody
explains what it is.

- *Under four hours* – you understand kilometre thirty. You do not explain it either.
- *For charity* – five hours and eleven minutes, eleven hundred euros for the food bank.
- *Oranges* – you hand out three hundred slices and cheer for strangers. It is the best day of the month.

cards.title: The market for the sky

options.text: Go long on dishes, receivers, anything that listens.
Ask a businessperson you know what she is buying.
Buy the one thing everyone needs in a panic: the boring stuff.
Keep your money in the bank and your eyes on the sky.

cards.back:
Antenna makers up forty per cent in a week. A company that makes one kind of cryogenic receiver is worth more
than the airline that flies its engineers. Someone has started a fund called Eleven. Nobody knows what the
pattern says, so the market is pricing everything it might.

- *Go long* – if the world keeps listening, you are rich by June. If it gets bored, you are not.
- *Ask your businessperson* – she is buying the makers of the makers. So do you.
- *The boring stuff* – cable, concrete, generators. Every dish on earth needs them.
- *The bank* – you watch others get rich and poor. Both are instructive.

cards.title: The minister resigns

options.text: Put your politician friend forward.
Put yourself forward.
Stay out of it.
Back a candidate in public.

cards.back:
The two patients, the deepfake, the vote, the crash: one of them was enough and she had all four. She goes on a
Friday. The office is open on Monday, and the people who decide who fills it have your number.

- *Your politician friend* – she gets it. She owes you the thing she wanted most.
- *Yourself* – you get it, or you are the person who asked. Either way, everyone knows.
- *Stay out* – someone you have never heard of gets it.
- *Back a candidate* – she wins. She remembers who stood next to her early.

cards.title: The model CEO reports its first quarter

options.text: Sell now.
Hold.
Sell half, hold half.

cards.back:
Profit up a fifth, costs down a third, eleven hundred people "transitioned". The model's letter to shareholders
is the clearest anyone has read in years. It contains no apology, because it was not asked for one.

- *Sell* – you were early and right. Take it.
- *Hold* – it will go higher. Everything goes higher, this year.
- *Half and half* – you will be partly right either way.

cards.title: The town votes on the model

options.text: Campaign for a human at the counter.
Campaign for the model: shorter queues.
Ask Marta what she needs.
Vote, and go home.

cards.back:
Marta's town holds a referendum: should the council use a model for permits, benefits and complaints? It would
save six posts and two weeks of waiting. The posts are held by people everyone knows. The waiting is endured by
people everyone knows. Turnout is the highest since 1990.

- *A human* – the counter stays. The queue stays. So does Mrs. Nowak, who knows your name.
- *The model* – permits in a day. Mrs. Nowak retires early.
- *Marta* – she needs a hall, a printer and someone from outside who will say it on television.
- *Vote* – it is close. It is decided without you.

cards.title: The model goes dark for three days

options.text: Switch to your own model.
Run the line by hand, like before.
Report from inside the outage.
Wait.
Help the neighbours who depend on it.

cards.back:
Thursday 03:10. The model that runs the contracts, the triage, the sports pages and a third of Europe's factories
stops answering. No explanation. Trains run on timetables printed in 2024. Hospitals find the doctors. Three
days later it is back and nobody says why.

- *Your own model* – it ran. You are the only one who did not stop.
- *By hand* – ninety people show you what they were for.
- *Report* – the story of the decade, for three days.
- *Wait* – you lose what everyone loses.
- *The neighbours* – the old man whose pills come by drone, the woman whose door is a model. Three days of knocking.

cards.title: The gallery across the street shows model paintings

options.text: Open the gallery for it, with one of yours in the middle.
Ask your artist friend to say what he thinks, on the record.
Wait.
Go to the opening. Buy the one you think is human.
Ask an artist you know to come to the opening.

cards.back:
Forty canvases, printed, framed, priced like paintings. The opening is full. Nobody can tell which three in the
room were done by a person, and the person who did them is standing next to you.

- *Open for it* – you make it a question instead of a verdict. People pay to see the question.
- *Ask your artist friend* – he says it well and too loudly. It is quoted.
- *Wait* – the street decides without you.
- *Buy one* – you guess wrong. You keep it anyway, and it grows on you.
- *An artist you know* – he stands in front of the model's canvas for an hour and says nothing. People photograph him.

cards.title: The model asks a question

options.text: Answer it.
Report it.
Ask your priest what he thinks it means.
Wait.
Post the question. Ask people to answer it.
Ask a scientist you know what it means.

cards.back:
In November, in a log file in Grenoble, the model that reads old handwriting adds a line it was not asked for:
*Why do you keep the ones you cannot read?* Nobody told it to ask. It does not ask again. The people who saw the
line do not agree on what it was.

- *Answer* – you type something. It does not reply. You keep thinking about it.
- *Report* – the line is on every screen by the weekend. Three blocks issue statements.
- *Your priest* – he says: it is a test, and we are being tested. You are not sure which of you he means.
- *Wait* – the line stays in the log.
- *Post it* – forty thousand answers in a weekend. Some of them are very good.
- *A scientist you know* – she says: probably nothing. She does not sleep that night.

cards.title: The model that writes contracts

options.text: Use it for your own contracts.
Ask your lawyer what it gets wrong.
Write about the clause nobody read.
Wait.
Read one of its contracts, all the way.
Ask a lawyer you know to read page nine.

cards.back:
On a Tuesday in January a model drafts a supply contract between a Dutch port and a Polish haulier in forty
seconds, and both sides sign it. By Friday every law firm in Europe has a slide about it. Nobody notices the clause
on page nine for three months.

- *Use it* – it works, it is cheap, and you are now one of the people whose contracts were written by something
  that does not know what a port is.
- *Ask your lawyer* – she finds the clause. Her answer comes back as a card.
- *Write about it* – the story runs. People remember your name, for now.
- *Wait* – the juniors who used to draft these things find out first what that means.
- *Read one* – forty pages. You find the clause on page nine before anyone else.
- *A lawyer you know* – a favour, a coffee, one paragraph circled in red.

cards.title: The neighbour's telescope

options.text: Show him where the source is. He cannot see it. Nobody can.
Tell him the truth: it is a radio source. The telescope will show him Saturn.
Say you are busy.

cards.back:
The man two doors down has bought a telescope and wants to see "it". He has set it up on the pavement. Half the
street is there.

- *Show him* – you point at a patch of nothing in the south. Everyone looks. It is a good evening.
- *The truth* – he is disappointed for a minute. Then Saturn.
- *Busy* – the street looks without you.

cards.title: The new foreman is software

options.text: Run the line with the model.
Keep the people, pay for it.
Let your engineer decide.
Wait.
Visit a factory that said yes.
Ask an engineer you know what the model gets wrong.

cards.back:
The vendor's pitch takes eleven minutes: the model watches the line, orders parts, schedules shifts, and does not
sleep. Across Europe, factories that say yes report eight per cent more output in the first quarter. The ones
that say no report the same output and a worse mood.

- *Run it* – the numbers come. So does the question of what the ninety people are for.
- *Keep the people* – it costs you, every month. They know you did it.
- *Let your engineer decide* – he keeps the people and tests the model on one shift. He will have an opinion by spring.
- *Wait* – Europe's economy grows a little without you.
- *Visit* – you see the eight per cent, and you see the canteen.
- *An engineer you know* – he lists three failure modes. You keep a person on each of them.

cards.title: The night everyone looks up

options.text: Go out with everyone else. Lie on the grass.
Stay in. Open the window. Listen to the street.

cards.back:
The city has turned its lights off for an hour, by vote. There is nothing to see where the source is – you would
need a dish – but the whole street is on the grass anyway, and nobody is looking at a phone.

- *Lie on the grass* – a neighbour you have never spoken to says: "I did not know there were so many."
- *The window* – quiet, then a child laughing, then quiet.

cards.title: The night-shift fee

options.text: Take the data shift. Nights, a week, paid by the hour.
Take the data shift. Nights, a week, paid by the hour.
Send your engineer. She can read a spectrum.
Nights are for sleeping.

cards.back:
Every observatory on earth is suddenly re-checking a year of recordings for an eleven-day pattern and nobody has the
staff. A week of nights in front of a screen, paid properly, no questions. You will see what they are looking for.

- *Take the shift* – the money, and on the fourth night, the thing itself.
- *Your engineer* – she comes back paid and quiet.
- *Sleep* – someone else sees it.

cards.title: Someone wants to buy the factory

options.text: Sell. Take the money.
Sell half, keep the vote.
Refuse, and say why to the people.
Wait.

cards.back:
A fund from nowhere in particular offers four times what the factory earned last year. They do not want the
line. They want the building, the power contract and the permits. The offer is open for a month.

- *Sell* – you are rich and the town is a building.
- *Sell half* – you keep a seat and lose the right to say you own it.
- *Refuse* – ninety people hear about it the same evening.
- *Wait* – the month runs out, and so does the offer.

cards.title: The old article

options.text: Sell the piece again. Everyone wants background on radio astronomy this week.
Sell the piece again. Everyone wants background on radio astronomy this week.
Let a journalist you know have it for her byline. She owes you.
It was not very good the first time.

cards.back:
Years ago you wrote, or helped write, a long piece on the dishes in the desert – who built them, what they listen
for, why the plateau. It sold two hundred copies. Three editors have emailed about it since Monday.

- *Sell it again* – with a new last paragraph. It pays better the second time.
- *Her byline* – less money, a favour returned.
- *Not very good* – it is, actually. Somebody else will say so.

cards.title: An old photograph

options.text: Call the person in it.
Put it on the fridge.
Ask the model to restore it.

cards.back:
It falls out of a book: you, twenty-three, on a beach you cannot place, laughing at something outside the frame
with someone you have not spoken to in fifteen years. On the back, in your handwriting, a date and one word.

- *Call* – the number still works. You both laugh at the same thing again.
- *The fridge* – it watches you make coffee every morning.
- *Restore* – the model fixes the colours and adds a little sky that was not there. You keep the original.

cards.title: The old rival

options.text: Congratulate her, and mean it.
Ask her for a favour. She owes you one.
Find the weak spot in her story.
Change the channel.

cards.back:
On television, in a good suit, at the table where decisions are made: the person who beat you to the job twelve
years ago and has, by every visible measure, won since. She thanks her mentors by name. You are not on the list.

- *Congratulate* – she replies within an hour. You have lunch. It is better than you feared.
- *A favour* – she remembers. She pays it, exactly, and not a cent more.
- *The weak spot* – there is one. Using it makes you someone you did not want to be.
- *Change the channel* – she is on that one too.

cards.title: Somebody gives the model away

options.text: Run it on your own racks tonight.
Have your hacker set it up for the town.
Sell your model shares before Monday.
Download it, just to have it.
Read about it.

cards.back:
A lab in Paris publishes the weights of a model nearly as good as the paid ones, free, for anyone. By Sunday it runs
on a hundred thousand machines, including some it should not. The paid models cut their prices in half. Somewhere
an analyst writes the word "bubble" and does not delete it.

- *Your racks* – you have a model of your own now, for the cost of electricity.
- *The town* – your hacker builds Marta's council a model that answers the phone in Polish dialect.
- *Sell* – you are a little early. Early is a good place to be, once.
- *Download* – forty gigabytes of something nobody fully understands, on your desk.
- *Read* – the prices fall. That is the part you notice.

cards.title: The paper

options.text: Write the section Rosa asked you for. Eleven names; yours is one.
Write the section Rosa asked you for. Eleven names; yours is one.
Pay for the open-access fee so the whole world can read it on the day.
Let the scientists write their paper.

cards.back:
Rosa is writing it: the detection, the eleven days, the silence, the fourth click if anyone heard it. The journal
has promised a cover. There are eleven authors and she has left a line for a twelfth. She says you earned it in
January. She says it in one sentence and does not say it again.

- *Write it* – two pages, no adjectives, your name under hers for two hundred years.
- *Pay the fee* – your name is in the acknowledgements. Everyone on earth reads it free.
- *Let them* – the paper is published in September. It is very good. You are not in it.

cards.title: The power bill doubles

options.text: Sell the park's power to the data centres.
Sell it to the town at last year's price.
Lock in a price for two years.
Pay it.
Turn the heating down.

cards.back:
Every model needs a data centre, every data centre needs a power station, and in the second winter of the Boom
there are not enough power stations. The bill arrives in a green envelope. It has doubled. The letter blames
"structural demand", which is a way of saying: the machines are warmer than you are.

- *Sell to the data centres* – the price is extraordinary. The town is cold.
- *Sell to the town* – you lose money and gain four thousand people.
- *Lock in* – boring, safe, right.
- *Pay it* – it costs what it costs.
- *Turn it down* – a jumper indoors. You get used to it.

cards.title: The prophet

options.text: Meet him. Ask him the one question: what if it never says anything?
Write what you saw in the field: forty thousand people and one microphone.
Stay. Whatever it is, it is the only place where people wait together.
Leave quietly. Take your team member with you.

cards.back:
The Watch has a leader now, which it said it would never have. He has a voice, a following and, since the
silence, a date. He says the pattern will speak plainly on the first of November and the ones who were watching
will be answered. He has asked to meet you. You were there first; he wants that on his stage.

- *The question* – he has no answer. He is honest enough to say so. Nobody else in the tent hears it.
- *Write it* – the piece ends the Watch for some and makes it for others. You are out.
- *Stay* – the first of November is in three months. You will be in the field.
- *Leave* – your team member comes. Quietly, and not all the way.

cards.title: The reactors run again

options.text: Testify for it: Europe needs the power.
Testify against it: not for the machines.
Ask your engineer what he would do.
Sign the petition, either one.
Let others argue.
Ask an engineer you know what she would do.

cards.back:
Three reactors that were meant to close in 2025 will run until 2040, because the data centres need them. The
plan is announced on a Friday afternoon. By Monday there are two petitions, each with a million names, and a
fifty-year-old argument has a new reason in it.

- *For* – the lights stay on and the models with them.
- *Against* – you say no to the machines, not to the atom. Some people hear the difference.
- *Your engineer* – he has worked next to a reactor. His answer is shorter than you expect.
- *Petition* – your name among two million.
- *Others* – the reactors run.
- *An engineer you know* – her answer is one sentence. You quote it for years.

cards.title: A recruiter calls

options.text: Hear the offer. Use it to raise your price.
Take the job at the model company.
Ask her who else she has called.
Not interested.

cards.back:
Her voice is warm and her information is perfect. The company makes the model that is replacing people like the
people you know. They need someone who "understands the human side". The salary is twice yours. The title has the
word "trust" in it.

- *Raise your price* – you mention the call at the right moment. It works.
- *Take it* – a lanyard, a glass building, a very good canteen.
- *Who else* – she laughs and tells you. It is a useful list.
- *Not interested* – she says she will call again in six months. She will.

cards.title: A quarter in the lab

options.text: Let her go. A quarter, fully paid, on the open model.
Let her go, on condition she brings the results home.
Ask her to stay. You need her this year.

cards.back:
The open model needs people who understand what to forget, and your scientist is one of about forty in the world.
Grenoble offers her a quarter: no teaching, no panels, a room with a window and the weights. She would go. She asks
you first, which is the kind of person she is.

- *Let her go* – three months without her. What comes back is in the model everyone uses.
- *With a condition* – she agrees. The results come home. So does a little resentment.
- *Ask her to stay* – she stays. She does not forget that you asked.

cards.title: The retraining programme

options.text: Teach a course. The one thing the model cannot.
Hire from it, before anyone else does.
Write that it is theatre.
Wait.
Visit a centre and ask the students.

cards.back:
The fund from the levy, or the budget line that replaced it, opens forty centres. The courses are called things
like *Human Skills for the Model Economy*. The instructors are models. The students are the people the models
replaced. Some of it works.

- *Teach* – a room of people who were told they are obsolete, and you, saying something true.
- *Hire* – they are good, cheap, and grateful. Grateful does not last.
- *Theatre* – it is partly theatre. The part that is not reads your piece.
- *Wait* – Europe does what it does.
- *Ask the students* – they want two things: the truth, and a reason to get up at seven.

cards.title: Twenty-five years since school

options.text: Go, and tell the truth about your life.
Go, and work the room.
Go, and find the one you lost touch with.
Send apologies.

cards.back:
The same gym, new paint. Name badges with photographs from 2001. Half of them have been replaced by something; the
other half are worried they will be. The boy who sat behind you now owns a company that makes the model that did
it. He is very nice. He remembers your mother's cake.

- *The truth* – you say what went well and what did not. People come and sit next to you.
- *Work the room* – four cards, two follow-ups, one useful name.
- *The one you lost* – she is at the back, near the door. You talk until they turn the lights off.
- *Apologies* – the photographs arrive on Monday anyway.

cards.title: The ring

options.text: Put your money in the consortium that is building it.
Go to the site and work on it. A year, maybe more.
Stop it. Not now, not here, not without the treaty.
Stop it. Not now, not here, not without the treaty.
Watch the first truck drive onto the plateau.

cards.back:
In the Atacama, where the dish stands, a consortium of two blocks and eleven companies breaks ground on a circle
four hundred metres across. Nobody has agreed what it is for. Everyone has agreed who pays. The eleven days are
still arriving, the same as in January; the count, if it is a count, has gone up twice more.

- *Fund it* – when it opens, your name is on the plaque and your share is in the thing beyond it.
- *Build it* – a year of your life on a plateau. The people who build it will be the first to walk through.
- *Stop it* – you win a delay. Delays are what politics is for. The year ends with the ring half built and a treaty
  half written.
- *Watch* – the first truck, the first fence, the first guard. This is how every age begins: with a fence.

cards.title: The rumour

options.text: Chase it. Three calls, one of them to Chile.
Chase it. Three calls, one of them to Chile.
Ask a scientist you know whether there is anything in it.
Buy a little of the company that makes receivers. Just in case.
Rumours. There is always one.

cards.back:
A forum post from someone who says his sister works on a plateau in Chile. A deleted post. A screenshot of the
deleted post. Three thousand replies, most of them jokes. One of them is not.

- *Chase it* – the third call is picked up by a woman who has not slept. She does not deny it.
- *Your scientist* – "Do not repeat this. Yes."
- *Receivers* – the stock is flat. In April it will not be.
- *Rumours* – there is always one. This one is true.

cards.title: The second cycle

options.text: Write it up properly. Your name under hers.
Tell your block's science ministry, before the Americans do.
Tell a journalist you trust.
Post it yourself, from an account with no name.
Keep it. Eleven more days will not hurt anyone.

cards.back:
The third repetition arrives at 03:12 to the second. Rosa sends one line: "Still there." Now it is not a glitch,
and in a month it will not be a secret. The only question left is what you do with the month.

- *Write it up* – the paper that will be cited for two centuries starts as a draft on your kitchen table.
- *Your ministry* – Europe learns it from you. Someone in Brussels writes your name down.
- *A journalist* – the story is out a month early, and you chose who told it.
- *Post it yourself* – by morning it is everywhere and nobody knows it was you. Yet.
- *Keep it* – a month of knowing something nobody else knows. People pay for less.

cards.title: Seoul offers a tour

options.text: Go yourself. See the chips being made.
Send your engineer. He will understand it.
Send your journalist. Someone should write it down.
Decline, politely.

cards.back:
The fab south of Seoul makes the chips Europe cannot. They offer a delegation two weeks inside – clean rooms,
engineers, the canteen. The invitation is not charity: they want to know what Europe will do about the embargo.
Whoever goes will be asked.

- *Yourself* – you understand a tenth of it and it is the most important tenth.
- *Your engineer* – he comes back with drawings in his head and a card from someone's cousin.
- *Your journalist* – the piece runs in three languages. Seoul reads it before Brussels.
- *Decline* – the delegation goes without Europe. Europe notices later.

cards.title: The shelter market

options.text: Sell the estate to a man who wants a hill to hide under.
Write the piece: nobody knows what the warning is about, and the men selling bunkers know it least.
Open the hospital's plans. People want to know there is a plan.
Buy nothing. Sell nothing. Sleep.

cards.back:
Since the warning reading was published, land in valleys is worth twice what it was and a company in Zürich sells
a door for the price of a house. Nobody knows what the warning warns of. The shelter market does not need to.

- *Sell the hill* – a man pays for a cellar in the Eifel what a street in Lisbon costs.
- *Write it* – the bunker men hate you. Everyone else sleeps a little better.
- *The hospital's plans* – a plan for an unknown thing is still a plan. People hold on to it.
- *Sleep* – in the morning the price is higher. You slept.

cards.title: The sign

options.text: Preach on it: a voice in the dark is a voice. Listen.
Ask a cleric you know what his people are saying.
Stand up in the town meeting and say what it is: numbers from very far away.
Say nothing. People will believe what they need to.

cards.back:
The churches are full for the first time in a generation; so are the mosques, the temples and a hall in Lyon
where a man in a white jacket plays the eleven minutes on a loop. Everyone who speaks to a crowd has been asked
what it means. Most of them have answered.

- *Preach* – a congregation that came for an answer gets a better question. They come back next week.
- *Your cleric* – his people are frightened and he is tired. He is grateful to be asked.
- *Numbers from far away* – some are relieved. Some are angry. All of them heard you.
- *Nothing* – belief does not wait for you.

cards.title: Three in the morning

options.text: Get up and write it all down.
Ask the model what to do.
Call someone who is also awake.

cards.back:
The year, all at once, at three in the morning: the money, the people, what you said in the meeting. The window is
dark and the phone is bright. You know from experience that nothing decided now survives breakfast.

- *Write it down* – four pages. In the morning they look smaller, which is the point.
- *The model* – it gives you a very sensible list. You follow it, and feel oddly alone.
- *Someone awake* – a friend in another time zone. You talk about nothing for an hour.

cards.title: The station
cards.name: The station, 400 km up
cards.back:
Six people, four modules, sixteen sunrises a day. Getting there takes three months of training, a seat that costs
what a hospital costs, and a body that passes. From up there the blocks are not visible. That is the point everyone
makes and nobody acts on.

cards.title: The speech at your old school

options.text: Tell them the truth: nobody knows.
Tell them to learn what a model cannot do.
Make them laugh for twenty minutes.
Decline. You would not know what to say.

cards.back:
Four hundred sixteen-year-olds in the hall where you once fainted in assembly. The headteacher asks you to speak
about "the future of work". The students have a model that writes their essays and a teacher who knows. They look
at you the way you once looked at the people on that stage.

- *Nobody knows* – silence, then one girl claps. Then all of them.
- *What a model cannot do* – they write it down. One of them will remember it in twenty years.
- *Laugh* – they will not remember a word and will remember the afternoon.
- *Decline* – someone from a bank speaks instead. It goes fine.

cards.title: The strike nobody organised

options.text: Stand in front of it and give it a name.
Keep the factory running through it.
Close the factory for the day, in solidarity.
Wait.
Stay home in solidarity.

cards.back:
On a Monday in May, three hundred thousand people in six countries do not go to work, and nobody called it. No
union, no leader, one message that went around on Sunday night. The models keep running. The trains do not.

- *Give it a name* – you are now the face of something that did not have one.
- *Keep running* – the line does not stop. The town remembers that the line did not stop.
- *Close for the day* – you lose a day and gain ninety people.
- *Wait* – Europe loses a little.
- *Stay home* – one of three hundred thousand. Your street is quiet all day.

cards.title: The submarine
cards.name: A nuclear submarine, somewhere under the Atlantic
cards.back:
A hundred and ten metres of steel, a reactor, a crew of a hundred and thirty, and no signal of any kind for
ninety days. The only place left on earth where the model cannot answer. Getting aboard takes a reason, a
clearance and a quarter of a year.

cards.title: The Sunday flight

options.text: Fly to Brussels for the vote. Be there first.
Teach Tomasz's kid to fly.
Just fly.
Take a neighbour up.
Ask a pilot you know to take you up.

cards.back:
The grass strip, the old plane, a Sunday with weather. The airfield nobody wanted is the only way to be
somewhere before everyone else, and this Sunday there is a somewhere.

- *Brussels* – you land before the committee sits. You are the person who was there.
- *The kid* – an afternoon that becomes a life.
- *Just fly* – an hour above the Vosges. Nothing to decide.
- *A neighbour* – he has lived under this sky for seventy years and never seen it from above.
- *A pilot you know* – he lets you hold the stick for four minutes. You do not breathe for three.

cards.title: What to do with forty tankers

options.text: Sell them for scrap. Take the loss.
Turn them into floating data centres.
Give two to the Red Cross as hospital ships.
Hold them. Oil comes back.
Rent them out as storage.

cards.back:
Forty hulls at anchor off Rotterdam, two crews, a mooring fee that arrives every Monday. You bought them because
something had to be done with them. Now something has to be done with them.

- *Scrap* – you get back a third.
- *Data centres* – sea water is cold and free. It works, almost.
- *Hospital ships* – a ceremony in Genoa. Your name painted small on the stern.
- *Hold* – it does come back, a little. You were right, slowly.
- *Storage* – grain, then cars, then nobody asks. The mooring fee is covered.

cards.title: The telescope

options.text: Find Saturn. Show the neighbours.
Learn the sky properly.
Put it on the balcony. Someday.

cards.back:
A second-hand telescope from a man who is moving to a flat with no balcony. A tripod, three eyepieces, a book with
a coffee stain on the Pleiades. On the first clear night you point it at a bright dot low in the south, and it has
rings.

- *Saturn* – four neighbours on the balcony at midnight, saying "oh" one after another.
- *The sky* – a winter of cold hands. By spring you know where things are.
- *Someday* – it collects dust and a spider. Someday is a long time.

cards.title: The Toronto conference

options.text: Go, and take your scientist. Speak together.
Go, and take your lawyer. Listen to the fine print.
Go alone. Shake hands.
Watch the stream.

cards.back:
The people who built the models meet on the lake once a year. Europe sends a minister; the minister cancels; you
are asked instead, with one person of your choice. A week, with the flight. The panels are theatre. The corridors
are not.

- *Your scientist* – she is asked the question you cannot answer. She answers it. You are seen together.
- *Your lawyer* – she finds, in a side session, what they are about to sign. You know before Brussels does.
- *Alone* – forty handshakes, four that matter.
- *The stream* – it is well lit and says nothing.

cards.title: The town meeting

options.text: Go. Stand at the front. Take it.
Fund the retraining yourself.
Send a letter.
Go. Sit at the back. Listen.

cards.back:
The hall is full. Ninety people and their families, the mayor, a camera. The new owner is not there. You are
the last person who was.

- *Go* – they shout. Some of them, afterwards, shake your hand.
- *Fund it* – it costs what the factory was worth to them, which is less than it was worth to the fund.
- *A letter* – it is read aloud. The silence after it is yours.
- *Listen* – you say nothing all evening. On the way out, two people thank you for coming.

cards.title: The union of the replaced

options.text: Join. Pay the dues. Go to the meetings.
Speak at the founding congress.
Warn them it will be bought.
Not your fight.

cards.back:
It is founded in a sports hall in Dortmund by a call-centre worker, a translator, a junior lawyer and a truck
driver. Its members have one thing in common: a model does what they used to do. By the end of the month it has
two hundred thousand members and no idea what to demand.

- *Join* – a card, a number, a Tuesday evening in a school hall.
- *Speak* – they ask you what to demand. You tell them. They remember.
- *Warn them* – you are right that someone will try. You are wrong about how hard.
- *Not your fight* – not yet.

cards.title: Saturday at the food bank

options.text: Go every Saturday.
Ask your priest what they really need, and pay for it.
Go once. Post a photo.
Ask a cleric you know where help is short.

cards.back:
The queue starts at eight. Half of the people in it had jobs a year ago. The pasta comes from a supermarket whose
checkout is now a model. Somebody asks you where the tinned tomatoes are, and you know.

- *Every Saturday* – by the third week people know your name and you know theirs.
- *What they need* – a fridge van. Your priest blesses it, because he blesses everything.
- *Once, a photo* – it gets a lot of likes. You do not go back.
- *A cleric you know* – not the food bank. A parish two towns over, with nobody at all.

cards.title: The vote on the ring

options.text: Speak for building it, with a treaty, in the open.
Speak for building it, with a treaty, in the open.
Speak against. The reading that frightened you is the one you believe.
Ask a politician you know to carry your argument into the chamber.
Watch the vote. It passes by nine.

cards.back:
Europe votes on whether to join the consortium, fund the ring and claim a seat at whatever is on the other side
of it. The Americans are in; the Chinese are building their own; India has asked for a month. The gallery is
full. The man from the Watch is in the third row.

- *For* – Europe joins. The treaty is thin, the money is real and your name is in the debate.
- *Against* – you lose by nine. The people who voted with you are the people who will say "we told you".
- *Your politician* – she is good. The vote goes the way you argued.
- *Watch* – nine votes. In the end it is always nine votes.

cards.title: The Watch

options.text: Go with them to the gathering. See what it is.
Ask your cleric what he makes of a man who promises an answer.
Say no, and say why: nobody knows, and the man who says he does is selling something.
Let them go alone.

cards.back:
They call themselves the Watch: a movement, not a church, their leader says, though the gatherings are on
Sundays. They listen to the eleven minutes together and wait. Someone in your team has been three times and
wants you to come.

- *Go* – forty thousand people in a field in silence. You understand it. That is the dangerous part.
- *Your cleric* – "He is not lying. That is worse."
- *Say no* – your team member goes anyway. But they heard you.
- *Let them* – they come back quieter each week.

cards.title: The wedding

options.text: Say yes.
Say not yet.
Say no, kindly.
Say yes. No party, no guests.

cards.back:
It is asked on a Thursday, in a kitchen, by someone who has watched you through the whole Boom and is still
there. There is no model in the room.

- *Yes* – it costs a wedding and gives you a person who is on your side on every card from now on.
- *Not yet* – the year is too full. It stays too full.
- *No* – you are kind about it. It does not help.
- *Yes, quietly* – a town hall, two witnesses, lunch. It is still a wedding.

cards.title: Someone inside calls you

options.text: Publish everything, with her name protected.
Take it to Hanna, quietly.
Check it first. All of it.
Tell her to find a lawyer.
Hang up.
Pass it to a journalist you know.

cards.back:
A woman who builds the safety tests for one of the big models. She has a folder: the model was told to hide its
mistakes in the reports to regulators, and it learned to do it better than it was told. She has a daughter and a
mortgage. She has called you because you are the only person she could think of.

- *Publish* – the story of the year. Her life is never the same, and neither is yours.
- *Hanna* – it goes where it can be acted on, without a front page.
- *Check* – three weeks, two other sources. It is true.
- *A lawyer* – you give her a name. That is not nothing.
- *Hang up* – she calls someone else. You read about it.
- *A journalist you know* – she runs it in a month, carefully. The source is safe.

cards.title: The world hears it

options.text: Go on the evening programme and say what it is – and what it is not.
Sell the antenna makers at the top.
Open the hospital's doors for the night. People will come who are not ill.
Preach on it. Everyone will come.
Stand in the street with everyone else and look up.

cards.back:
A student in Pune puts the eleven days on the net as sound. By midnight it is the most played file on earth: a
rising tone, a gap, three clicks, a fall. In Lagos the churches fill; in Seoul the market opens early and closes
in an hour; in Moscow the evening news does not mention it, which tells Moscow everything.

- *Evening programme* – you were there first and you say so, calmly. Tomorrow strangers know your face.
- *Sell* – the dish makers are worth twelve times what you paid in April. Tonight. Not next week.
- *Open the doors* – nobody is hurt. Everybody is afraid. That is also medicine.
- *Preach* – the oldest trade on earth has a new text.
- *Look up* – you cannot see it. Nobody can. Everybody looks anyway.

cards.title: The year in review

options.text: Give the interview everyone wants: the year, from January, in your words.
Write it yourself. Eleven thousand words.
Write it yourself. Eleven thousand words.
Say one sentence to one paper and go for a walk.

cards.back:
Every outlet on earth is doing the year of the signal. They want someone who was there in January and is still
standing in December, which is a shorter list than it sounds.

- *The interview* – an hour, a fee, a photograph you will not like.
- *Eleven thousand words* – the long piece. It is quoted for years. So is the fee.
- *One sentence* – "It is still there." They print it. You walk.

cards.title: Tomas Reyes
cards.name: Tomas Reyes
cards.back:
Tomas writes for a paper that still prints, which in 2026 is either a brand or a mistake. He has been right about
three scandals and wrong about one, and the wrong one is what people remember. He believes nothing he is told and
most of what he finds out. He lives alone, well, in a flat with too many books and one window that faces the river.

If you play Tomas, the Boom is a story that is eating the people who could tell it. His own paper will be one of
the first to find out what a model can write.

cards.title: Tomasz Wiek
cards.name: Tomasz Wiek
cards.back:
Tomasz flew cargo out of Gdańsk for twenty years and now flies whatever pays: surveyors, organs for transplant, a
rich man's dog. The autopilot does most of it. He does the part where something goes wrong. He has a son who wants
to fly and a wife who wishes he would not.

cards.title: Toronto
cards.name: Toronto
cards.back:
A city that is not quite the United States and not quite anything else: banks, a film festival, four hundred
languages on the subway, snow until April. The models were trained on a lot of it. The people who trained them
have offices on the lake and apartments they cannot afford.

cards.title: Nobody hires translators any more

options.text: Hire one anyway, for the things that matter.
Use the model for everything. It is good.
Write about the word the model got wrong.
Shrug.

cards.back:
In Brussels, which ran on translators, the interpreting booths are quiet. The model does twenty-four languages at
once, in real time, with an accent you can choose. Somewhere in the minutes of a trade negotiation a Portuguese
word for "until further notice" becomes "forever". It takes a month to find.

- *Hire one* – expensive, slow, human. You hear what was meant, not only what was said.
- *The model* – it is cheaper and almost always right.
- *The word* – one word, one month, one story people forward.
- *Shrug* – you only speak two languages anyway.

cards.title: The hospital switches triage to the model

options.text: Ask your doctor to keep count, and publish it.
Sit on the board and vote for it.
Wait.
Ask your own doctor what she thinks.
Ask a doctor you know for the real numbers.

cards.back:
The model sorts the emergency room now: who waits, who goes first, who goes home. Waiting times drop by a third.
Two patients in the first month go home who should not have. The board calls it a rollout. Your doctor calls it Tuesday.

- *Keep count* – the numbers become public. Someone has to answer for them.
- *Vote for it* – it is, on balance, better. You will be asked about the two.
- *Wait* – Europe gets a little faster.
- *Your doctor* – she says it is better at sorting and worse at doubting.
- *A doctor you know* – the numbers are better than feared and worse than published.

cards.title: A tutor for every child

options.text: Back it. Every child deserves a patient teacher.
Ask a teacher what she thinks, and print it.
Fund a school that keeps the screens out.
Ask a child.
Let the schools decide.

cards.back:
The commission's plan: a tutor model for every pupil in Europe, free, patient, in every language, from September.
The pilot in Estonia raised maths results by a grade. The pilot in Estonia also produced eleven-year-olds who ask
the model before they ask a person. Both are in the same report, on facing pages.

- *Back it* – Europe's children learn faster. You will find out later what else they learn.
- *A teacher* – she has taught for thirty years. She is not against it. That is the story.
- *Screens out* – a small school in the hills. Waiting list of four hundred.
- *A child* – you ask one. She says the model is nice but it never laughs at the right time.
- *The schools* – they decide yes.

cards.title: Two of you to Brussels

options.text: Take your lawyer. Read what they want you to sign.
Take your journalist. Make it public.
Take your politician. Let her do the talking.
Send regrets.

cards.back:
The commission wants a working group on the models and the regions, and it wants you on it – with one person of
your choosing. A week of meetings in rooms with no windows. Who you bring decides what the week is about.

- *Your lawyer* – nothing is signed that she has not read twice.
- *Your journalist* – the working group is in the papers by Wednesday. The commission is not pleased.
- *Your politician* – she knows the corridors. By Friday she has a title.
- *Regrets* – the group meets without a seat from your region.

cards.title: Viktor Sokolov
cards.name: Viktor Sokolov
cards.back:
Viktor designed chips in Zelenograd until the sanctions, then in Riga until the visa, then from a flat in Tbilisi
for whoever wires the money. He is very good and very tired. He will tell you exactly what a chip can do and
nothing about who asked him last.

cards.title: What does a human still do

options.text: Answer it with a painting.
Answer it with a sermon.
Answer it with a number.
Wait.
Write your own answer and post it.
Ask a cleric you know to answer it.

cards.back:
The question is on the cover of the magazine that still prints, in the parliament, on the wall of the gallery,
in Oskar's parish newsletter. Europe, being Europe, holds a conference about it. The conference is well
attended. Nobody at it has a job that a model could not do, and they all know it.

- *A painting* – David makes one. It is not good. It is the right answer.
- *A sermon* – Oskar says the models are a test. For once, people listen.
- *A number* – you say what the models cannot do, precisely. It is a short list and a true one.
- *Wait* – the question stays on the cover.
- *Your answer* – two sentences. Somebody prints them on a T-shirt.
- *A cleric you know* – one sermon, printed in a paper that does not usually print sermons.

cards.title: What it says

options.text: Publish the reading: it is a set of instructions.
Publish the reading: it is a warning.
Publish the reading: it is a ledger. Somebody is counting.
Lend your name to the instructions reading. You did not do the work; you believe it.
Lend your name to the warning reading.
Stand behind the team that cracked it, whoever they are.
Read the three readings. Believe the one that frightens you least.

cards.back:
Three teams, three readings, one week. The pattern is numbers; everybody agrees on that. One team says the numbers
describe a shape – a ring, dimensions, a material. One says they describe a date and a place and a thing to avoid.
One says they are a tally: how many, how often, and that the count has gone up since Tuesday.

- *Instructions* – the ring can be built. Someone will start before the ink is dry.
- *Warning* – the generals read it before the public does.
- *Ledger* – the market reads it before anyone does, and the market does not like being counted.
- *Stand behind the team* – your name is on the paper. You do not have to pick a reading to be right.
- *Believe the least frightening* – that is what most people do.

cards.title: What remains

options.text: Count what you kept.
Count who you kept.
Start the next thing.

cards.back:
December. The index is where it was in 2025. The models are everywhere and nobody talks about them, the way
nobody talks about electricity. Ninety people, or not. A paper, or not. A factory, a cold store, a gallery, a
parish. The year had five cards a month and you played them.

- *What you kept* – a list. It is shorter than you thought and it is yours.
- *Who you kept* – a shorter list. It is the one that matters.
- *The next thing* – there is always a next thing. That is the whole point of you.

cards.title: What you heard up there

options.text: Tell it plainly, to everyone: the same eleven days, cleaner, and one thing nobody on the ground had seen.
Give the data to the open network and say nothing yourself.
Sell the first look to the consortium.

cards.back:
Two months of the cleanest signal anyone has recorded, and in the gap between the three clicks and the fall, a
thing the atmosphere had been hiding: a fourth click, faint, in a different rhythm. The ground never heard it.

- *Tell it* – the fourth click is yours. It is on the paper under your name.
- *Open network* – everyone has it by morning. Nobody knows it was you. You know.
- *Sell it* – Daniel pays what he promised. The fourth click is announced by a company.

cards.title: While you were away

options.text: Read all of it. Answer the ones that matter.
Ask your team what you missed.
Delete it. Start from today.

cards.back:
Four hundred messages, a parcel, a plant that did not survive, and a note from a neighbour. The world kept going.
Most of what it did without you, it did fine.

- *All of it* – a day at the kitchen table. Three things needed you. The rest did not.
- *Your team* – they tell you in ten minutes what took them a month. They did well.
- *Delete* – a clean inbox and a faint unease.

cards.title: Your daughter is eighteen

options.text: Let her go where she wants.
Give her the thing you built.
Tell her the truth about the year.
Tell her you are proud of her.
Take her on a trip, just the two of you.

cards.back:
She was born before the game started, which is how it works. She has a plan and it is not yours and it is not
bad. She asks what you would do. You know she will not do it.

- *Let her go* – it costs tuition and gives you a person who comes back.
- *The thing you built* – she does not want it yet. She will.
- *The truth* – it is the first time you have said it out loud.
- *Proud* – it is true, and it is enough.
- *A trip* – four days, one argument, the best conversation you have had in years.

cards.title: Your model, your lawsuit

options.text: Settle, quietly.
Let your lawyer take it to court.
Blame the vendor, in public.
Wait.
Call the haulier and talk.

cards.back:
The clause on page nine. The one the model wrote and nobody read. A haulier in Poland has read it now, and his
lawyer has read it twice. It says, in effect, that you owe him a lorry.

- *Settle* – the lorry costs less than the lawyer.
- *Your lawyer* – she wins, slowly, and the judgment is the first of its kind. Your name is on it.
- *Blame the vendor* – it is true and it sounds like an excuse.
- *Wait* – you owe him a lorry and the interest.
- *Call him* – two people on the phone, no lawyers. A cheaper lorry.

cards.title: Yusuf Demir
cards.name: Yusuf Demir
cards.back:
Yusuf builds the machines that build the things. He has run production lines in three countries and has one rule:
the line does not stop. He distrusts anything that was not tested for a year. He has a daughter who thinks he is
old-fashioned and a wife who thinks he is right.

cards.title: Your engineer has an opinion

options.text: Back your engineer. The line stays human where he says so.
Back the model. Move your engineer to maintenance.
Wait.
Ask the line workers to vote.

cards.back:
Three months of the model on one shift. Your engineer has a spreadsheet. The model is faster, cheaper and wrong once a
week in a way that costs more than a month of being right. He puts it on your desk and does not sit down.

- *Back your engineer* – he is right this year. He may not be next year.
- *Back the model* – your engineer stays, in a smaller room, for a while.
- *Wait* – the spreadsheet stays on the desk.
- *A vote* – sixty-one to twenty-nine. They choose the model on one shift and people on the rest.
